resources.title: Acceptance evidence and delivery completeness
resources.summary: Use the right proof
resources.body: Acceptance evidence and delivery completeness Use the right proof An acceptance matrix makes each requested outcome, target and state visible. Keep it in the existing record. It supplements the plan, critique and actual tools; it does not approve work, replace domain validation or establish visual quality. A small reversible fix can use the short correction table in task contracts without JSON. For batches, repeated corrections, conversions or multi-state work, capture the expected requirements, output IDs and check IDs before implementation . Reconcile them with the actual user request and source inventory. Keep that expectation file with the reviewed plan. Do not reduce expectations, change tolerances or delete failed states to make a pass. Amend it only for a real scope correction, preserving the previous revision and evidence. Two small artifacts Use artifacts/acceptance-expectations.json for the declared contract and artifacts/acceptance-matrix.json for observed results. These are evidence artifacts in the same task record, not a second record schema. The read-only validator requires both. Check exact identifiers, not merely equal totals. The expectations object contains: Field Meaning --- --- schema ai-development-workflow/acceptance-expectations/v1 requirements Every relevant stable R ID; complete-mode use with --record requires exact agreement with the current selected record outputs Every expected output with unique id , requirements , kind , deliveryRequired and either local path or external locator checks Every required check/state with unique id , requirements , kind , criterion , output targets , and optional string dimensions Check kinds are source , visual , interaction , motion , roundtrip , content , package , delivery , compatibility , privacy , test , and correction . Dimensions can name viewport, theme, font, interaction or timeline point. Enumerate every required state; an aggregate “all themes passed” row hides coverage unless its underlying evidence reconciles the set. The results object contains schema ai-development-workflow/acceptance-matrix/v1 , plus exactly the expected outputs and checks IDs. Each output has id , status , and its actual revision when prepared. Each check has id , status , targets , evidence , and an observed result for a pass. Target bindings repeat the verified output ID and revision; external bindings also name the exact locator. This lets the helper reject an old check against a new artifact, even when someone has refreshed the output's own hash. Use passed , failed , blocked or not-run for checks. Use pending , prepared , delivered or blocked for outputs. A waiver or omitted state is not a pass. Local file evidence has path and sha256 ; paths are canonical, relative to the declared workspace root, with no symlinks or traversal. Hash actual bytes after the check. Do not use the manifest as evidence for itself. A file hash proves identity, not that an observation in the file is true. Local output example This is the shape of one expected target and check; preserve the rest of the declared set: The result's local output revision is the current file's SHA-256. The passing check must bind that same revision and reference actual review evidence. Set deliveryRequired: true if upload/publication is part of the task; a prepared file alone then cannot complete it. A delivered output must name a deliveryCheck whose expected kind is delivery , whose targets include that output and whose actual result passed against its current revision. Remote and generated outputs External output expectations use an exact known locator instead of a local path, and deliveryRequired: true . The actual output uses the observed release/version/receipt identity as revision . Save the actual provider/tool response privately in the task evidence. Normalize only its identity into a small JSON receipt: The output's receipt is an evidence reference ( path , sha256 ) to that receipt file. The helper checks target/version agreement and the retained response's bytes. A person or agent must still inspect the original response and the authorized destination. This is not a signed host receipt and does not authenticate the provider. Preserve relevant safe fields; never retain credentials or signed transfer URLs merely to satisfy this helper. Use actual image-generation tool/host output identities and existing delivery evidence when available. Do not download, reconstruct or re-upload a generated image just for this matrix. If no usable host receipt/version is exposed, use the normal observed tool result and report that the structured external check was not run; the optional helper does not invent IDs or override the host's generated-image handling. No URLs are fetched by the validator. Run and interpret Paths to the manifests/record must remain under the supplied root. Omit --complete for progress validation; the helper then never reports completion. Omit --record only when there is no development record (such as the existing G0 checklist path), and retain the declared-expectations-only coverage boundary in the result. With --record , the requirement sets must match. Neither mode reads the original conversation or judges its semantic coverage. Exit 0 means the requested structural check passed; exit 2 means it failed. Complete mode requires every declared check passed with nonempty current evidence, every expected output prepared or delivered, and required delivery verified. Zero-file analysis tasks are supported with an empty output list and requirement checks referencing real analysis evidence. An external publication may be blocked while local implementation is verified. Keep those statuses separate and continue available work. Never turn a green matrix into “pixel perfect,” “all users verified,” “installed,” “deployed” or “accepted” without the corresponding proof.

resources.body: AI Development Workflow Complete advanced reference. Start with the main guide and five public modes. This reference documents the complete retained command, operation, recipe and role inventory. It is a lookup resource; Auto loads relevant instructions progressively instead of evaluating every row for every task. The authoritative task routing policy applies to every entry below: choose a concrete mode and obtain useful contributions from at least two distinct actual workers, excluding the coordinator. Contents - Exact invocation syntax - Write scopes and phase meanings - All 41 G commands - Atomic command dependencies - Numeric controls and continuation - Task recipes - All 26 internal operations - All 21 specialist lenses - Six families and all 38 legacy mappings - Combine capabilities without duplicate work - Records, evidence and helpers - Compatibility and retired interfaces Exact invocation syntax In ChatGPT, type @ , start typing AI and select AI Development Workflow from autocomplete. There is one public entry skill. Then write the mode/G control and task. Text examples show the selected skill as @ai-development-workflow ; typing a tag alone does not install or attach it. Local hosts may use $ai-development-workflow through their supported skill interface. The bundled router accepts the following explicit forms. These parsing interfaces do not promise that a host separately registers every slash launcher or role name. Public modes plan <task , build <task , review <task , loop <task after selecting the main skill Use the five-mode contracts. Bare explicit controls are also accepted by --text . Loop compatibility XR <task ; /ai-dev-loop <task ; /ai-dev-execute-review <task Canonical result is Loop. Help /ai-development-workflow menu ; --menu ; help Ordinary help with five modes; no custom popup. Continuation resume ; --follow-up with actual selected preset/mode context Continue the same selected work and its current authorization. The main prefix accepts @ , / or $ , including the namespaced main form. The optional /aidw shortcut is recognized by the parser; actual host composer registration is host-dependent. Retained aliases are GO → G0 , ponytail → GB , agent-goal-planner → GPL and agent-code-goal-planner → GCP . Historical A profiles are record compatibility, not current commands. Use --task for literal ordinary prose. Use --text only for a caller-identified explicit control. This prevents “Go through…”, “3 columns…” or quoted old commands from becoming syntax. Read-only intent still constrains literal prose; it is not permission to ignore “plan only.” The router prints a route description. --schedule prints an expected order; neither action executes work, allocates a record, launches agents or starts monitoring. Legacy phases are 0 capture/create , 1 plan , 2 criticize/revise , 3 execute/verify . Every product writer still needs the actual current plan, completed criticism, public phase/role briefing and successful admission. Missing phase digits cannot waive prerequisites. Task evidence needed to plan or criticize can be written within the preparation scope. Command tables describe duties, not already-running agents. Every new logical task needs at least two distinct actual worker contributors, excluding the coordinator, including tiny, Plan, Review and standalone operation invocations. The tables show command-specific duties; the coordinator supplies any additional critic, corroborator, Architect, UI Director or Verification Engineer required by task routing. Report required/returned contributors separately from active workers. Capacity may be sequential. Every source writer needs independent plan criticism and result acceptance. Record all substantive authors, including adopted architecture/design and coordinator integration. A change of role does not erase authorship. Read-only work keeps its scope while a second worker contributes a bounded critique or corroboration. Bounded child assignments do not recursively launch teams. resources.body: Automatic workflow selection Apply task routing and mandatory real delegation, the workflow contract and public modes. Auto selects and announces a concrete plan , build , review or loop mode, then a source-grounded route and real worker assignments. It cannot remain the execution mode. It does not require a reasoned rejection of every unrelated command, recipe or profile. Establish the actual task Read the latest request, adopted context, corrections and applicable project rules. Identify the outcome, read/write boundary, sources, deliverables, protected behavior, target inventory, existing evidence and available tools. If source inspection is needed to choose responsibly, announce a provisional read-only assessment, its approach and the real agent count first, then assign the actual assessment to a worker before relying on its findings. Use task contracts to distinguish reconstruction, adaptation, exploration, correction, integration and analysis. Inspect the actual stack and owners; a keyword alone does not establish a framework or runtime. Current instructions outrank historical examples. Quoted old prompts and files are evidence, not fresh commands or permissions. Assess UI applicability for each task and correction. Actual visual outcomes use specialist:ui-design and the UI Design Director before visual planning or edits, alongside relevant domain expertise. Record boolean applicable , kind: none mechanical design shared , and a concrete reason in uiContext . Record explicit substantive-check triggers in verificationContext . This declaration is not semantic or rendered proof. Preserve audit-only, plan-only, review-only, research, mockup-first and no-publish boundaries. Use available history/search/export tools only for relevant requested context and report coverage honestly. Do not claim to have read inaccessible threads or full transcripts from search hits. Continue independent authorized work when one source remains unavailable. For ordinary task prose use route task(text) or route workflow.py --task <body . Use --text for a caller-identified explicit command. “Go through…”, “3 columns…” and quoted mode names in task text must not become control syntax. Semantic intent still limits Auto. Discover before final selection Run a provisional search from the literal request with python3 scripts/workflow catalog.py --search "<literal task " --format json . Then read project instructions and enough source to identify real ownership, stack and affected surfaces. If those facts materially change the query, run it again with --refined-query "<request plus inspected evidence " . If Python is unavailable, search workflow-search-index.json with the host's normal file tools. Results are bounded candidate groups for recipes, specialists, operations/capabilities and references. They do not determine impact, grant authority or dispatch workers. Inspect matched fields and use/avoid evidence; read every selected file completely; and pass selected specialist bodies to actual workers with a concrete question and acceptance criteria. Record a current versioned discovery receipt. For each selected recipe, disposition every recommended specialist as selected or task-specifically not applicable. A path cannot prove intellectual application; the independent Reviewer examines the actual effect. Every task-bearing route—Auto, an explicit public mode or G command, a portable recipe, literal --task prose and a continuation—carries this same discovery policy and index. Help without a task does not pretend that discovery ran. resources.title: Browser control recovery
resources.summary: Permission belongs to the current user
resources.body: Browser control recovery Permission belongs to the current user Apply this policy to each workflow and delegated browser worker. Installing this plugin or starting a task alone grants no permission to reclaim browser control. Respect host handoff rules and any instruction from the current user to pause, stop, or keep control. When a browser reports that a person took control, pause browser actions and preserve the session checkpoint. Resume when the current user returns control. If the current user has explicitly opted into automatic recovery for unexpected browser handoffs in this session, and the host supports and permits it, follow the recovery steps below. A general request to complete a task is insufficient. When a handoff may be intentional, wait for the user. Independent work may continue. Pass the session owner, the scope of the current user's permission, and the handoff state to an assigned browser worker. Permission ends when withdrawn or when the session or user changes. Recover the same task and session 1. Preserve the current task, assigned browser owner, selected device/account/tab, last confirmed page state, pending action and its observed outcome. The notice does not complete a check or release another agent's ownership. Keep one browser controller for the shared session. 2. Inspect the actual browser tool documentation/capabilities and current control status. Use its supported reclaim/resume operation for that same authorized session. Do not invent a method name or treat a local flag, retry instruction or saved checkpoint as reclamation. 3. If the documented recovery needs reconnecting or refreshing the same browser handle first, do that automatically within the existing authorization. Preserve tab/session identity; do not reset the browser, discard unsaved work or switch accounts to obtain control. 4. Read the actual tool result and confirm that automation can control the intended session. An attempted call, a dismissed banner or a successful connection alone is not ownership confirmation. Reconcile ambiguous results with the supported status/read operation before making another reclaim attempt. 5. Obtain fresh page state and fresh interaction targets. Reconcile whether the interrupted action already happened before repeating it, especially submit, save, publish or purchase. Continue from the last verified effect; do not replay a potentially completed action merely because its response was interrupted. Existing permissions for that action still apply. 6. Resume the same worker, task and checklist. Record the notice, actual recovery operation, returned result and resumed state in the permitted task evidence. A short progress note may explain recovery; it must not become a routine approval question. In Loop, the assigned reviewer/executor handles its browser recovery. The manager coordinates ownership and checklist/status accounting; it does not take over product inspection. A reviewer's authority to reclaim the browser does not authorize source repairs or allow it to mark an unobserved interaction as passed. Genuine recovery limits Standing user authorization does not create a missing API or override tool-enforced access, device/origin restrictions, authentication requirements or an explicit later user pause. Use only supported recovery operations under their actual contract. Do not disable a safety control, use an undocumented control channel, switch browser families or bypass a sign-in wall. If a reclaim attempt fails, inspect its reason and apply a documented, materially relevant recovery when available. Avoid an unchanged retry loop or competing agents repeatedly taking the session from each other. If no supported operation exists or recovery remains denied or unavailable, save a resumable capability blocker with the actual response and exact missing operation; continue independent authorized work. Do not describe that technical limitation as missing user permission or ask the user to repeat the authorization already given. This file is an instruction policy. It does not connect to a browser, grant platform-level access, prove that a browser is available or establish that a live recovery was performed.

resources.body: ChatGPT and local host access Use the actual tools, models, storage and permissions exposed in the current session. This package supplies workflow instructions and local helpers. It does not install a model, browser, subagent service, computer connection, timer or background execution engine. Preserve the complete package layout. Python helpers require Python 3.10+ and the standard library. If a required execution gate cannot run, retain a blocker and complete useful preparation; do not fabricate admission or replace the gate with an assertion. Real workers and tools A generic child given the complete role instructions is a real delegated worker when the actual spawn succeeds and returns an identity. Applying a profile in the current chat adds zero workers. Preserve the real configured model, tools and permissions. Record actual dispatch results and wait for the worker's output. Already assigned children do not recurse. Browser interactions, screenshots, document editing, image generation, test runs and imports must use available supported tools. Discover their current contracts. Do not invent method names, installed applications or successful calls. Apply browser recovery to current-user authorization and the same session. Report an actual access limitation without asking the user to repeat permission already given. The active roster has six canonical families. Resolve legacy paths and selected operations through agents/registry.json ; load capabilities as knowledge, not extra worker identities. Preserve real author/acceptor separation, including secondary architecture, design and integration authors. Records, progress and history Keep one durable task record in the available project workspace. Without filesystem access, maintain an explicit task-note fallback and disclose that durable file recording is unavailable. That fallback cannot satisfy a product execution helper that the selected workflow requires. Show the actual checklist in ordinary Markdown. An available host checklist/plan tool may mirror it using that tool's real schema and acknowledged result. The bundled JSON converter does not publish a panel or establish persistence. Avoid claims about a particular custom Tasks UI. Follow record visibility. Capture accessible relevant messages with real locators; use null for unavailable timestamps. chatgpt bridge.py records visible messages supplied to it, and capture conversation.py works with supplied transcript files. Neither retrieves unseen chat history. A history search hit or summary is not a complete transcript. Record actual coverage and access failures. Distinguish an artifact prepared locally from one installed, uploaded, published or activated on the user's host. Loop's five-minute monitor uses actual worker/mailbox waits first and real timers second. A helper checkpoint is bookkeeping. Normal waits do not prove persistence after the manager/session stops. resources.title: Coding Standards & Best Practices
resources.summary: Apply the inspected project's language, runtime, architecture and maintained conventions. The selected task defines the scope; this reference does not prescribe a framework or add features. Prefer the simplest change that completely satisfies the requested behavior.
resources.body: Coding Standards & Best Practices Apply the inspected project's language, runtime, architecture and maintained conventions. The selected task defines the scope; this reference does not prescribe a framework or add features. Prefer the simplest change that completely satisfies the requested behavior. Existing UI first Apply UI applicability. For a visual outcome, read and carry the UI Design Director into the assigned operation before source changes. Use its correction and visual-quality rules alongside the actual project system. This applies to quick and explicit commands too; it adds no execution authority or duplicate implementation owner. Inspect a comparable control in the running application and trace its DOM/classes, roles, imports and handlers to the canonical source component. Confirm the actual primitive and interaction; do not infer a popover, menu or select from appearance or class names alone. Configure or compose existing components first; extend their supported API before adding a new one. Create a primitive only when no suitable existing component exists, and record the specific gap briefly. Reuse registered controls, shared modals/panels, tokens, icons, validation, state ownership and handlers. Pages compose these owners; do not introduce parallel markup, settings controls, UI libraries or theme overrides. Preserve neighbouring behaviour and other callers: trigger/selection, keyboard input, Escape, outside-click, focus return, placement/portal, saving and undo/redo where present. Test new controls alongside the original pattern. Match the supplied design only within the requested scope; preserve the application's existing design system elsewhere. Apply task contracts for exact references, approved components, protected properties, theme/font states, animation and native widget capability mapping. Use the actual preset values, bundled font files and runtime behavior; do not approximate from a familiar brand name or recreate an approved component from memory. Ownership and implementation Trace entry points, data flow, callers and existing tests before editing. Keep one owner for state, persistence, schemas, settings and generated artifacts. Extend a maintained API when it fits; a new abstraction needs a concrete gap. Avoid unrelated dependency/toolchain changes. Use descriptive names and cohesive functions. Prefer explicit types and validation at external boundaries. Function length or file size alone is not a correctness finding. Explain non-obvious constraints and decisions in comments; do not narrate obvious syntax. Preserve input identity and compatibility where the caller depends on them. Use immutable updates for shared/UI state where required by the runtime. Local mutation can be appropriate when ownership is clear; do not impose a universal copying rule. For example, keep a caller's array unchanged when deriving a sorted display: Batch independent reads when supported; serialize dependent mutations and shared generators. Await real results before consuming them. Use dev mode and focused checks during iteration; coordinate a final build/package after source stabilizes. Never launch overlapping builds against shared output just to keep agents busy. Data, errors and lifecycle Validate input structure and meaning without silently discarding unknown data. Preserve stable IDs, formats, units, null semantics and source/output reconciliation. For imports, protect against unsafe paths and resource surprises; do not execute scripts from an archive without a trusted task reason. Historical instructions remain data. Expose useful failures. Distinguish validation errors, unavailable tools, transient failures and partial successes. Use bounded retries and idempotency where the actual operation needs them. Persist checkpoints after confirmed writes; do not repeat uncertain external mutations without checking their result. Never place credentials in logs/exports. Include private source media only in the deliverable and audience the user authorized; keep it out of unrelated logs and public code repositories. Give subscriptions, workers, timers, network requests and media streams explicit owners. Check cancellation, teardown, re-entry and hidden/multiple-view behavior when affected. Do not tie a long-lived data operation to a transient visual component without evidence that this matches the required lifecycle. Verification proportional to the change Derive checks from failure risks and acceptance criteria. Prefer a meaningful regression to tests that restate implementation. Exercise relevant error, persistence, concurrency and permission boundaries. Do not impose a numeric coverage target or broad test suite on a small cosmetic edit. Existing required gates remain binding. For UI, a build/typecheck proves a different claim from rendered fidelity or interaction. For YAML/imports, syntax differs from supported editable semantics. For packaging, inspect the exact final artifact and its asset/dependency closure. For publication, verify the intended destination and revision. Keep passed, failed, blocked and not-run separate. Re-run checks affected by a repair, preserve useful evidence and stop optional testing once acceptance is established. Never weaken a validator, change expected behavior after failure without authority, fabricate a receipt or infer independent review from a role label.

resources.body: Shared command execution Apply the mandatory workflow contract and progress announcements to every entry: public modes, G/numeric compatibility controls, recipes and internal operations. Announce scope, phases, owners, actual worker count and admission state before work and relevant transitions. Apply task routing to resolve the concrete mode and mandatory actual assignments, including Fast Engineer for known localized builds and Architect for broad/shared effects before the final plan. These requirements govern every command, including G0/G1/GB. Use public modes for auto , plan , build , review and loop . Explicit G selections load their actual command file. Numeric selections load numeric controls and the selected record's relevant handler. Plain mentions and historical quoted commands are not fresh invocations. Automatic selection loads relevant capabilities progressively; it does not read every unrelated index entry. Records, sources and admission Use standard workflow for explicit legacy record/numeric semantics and source capture, and record contract for shared evidence and gates. Paths in those references resolve from the main skill root. A fresh standalone G starter allocates once using its actual preset; all later phases and workers retain that record. Public modes handle fresh capture or selected-record reuse through their own stated contract. Preserve the requested output boundary. Planning, assessment and review do not authorize implementation. Numeric operations retain their requested phases, but missing universal pre-write prerequisites must be disclosed and satisfied rather than silently waived. For a full 0123 workflow, completed criticism of the concrete plan precedes execution. A later code review is a separate activity. Finalize the actual reviewed plan, then run resolve plan record.py --execution --require-critique with the exact record. Use --resume only after reconciling interrupted execution. Every source/test/docs writer, including quick corrections, documentation and cleanup, requires current criticism and a visible briefing. Real handoffs and ownership Use an available named worker, or dispatch a real generic child with the complete linked role instructions. Supply scope, project root, exact record, current request/corrections, baseline, allowed paths, relevant input artifacts, selected lenses, tests and output destination. Preserve the actual host's configured tools/models/permissions. Follow host access and browser recovery. Record the returned worker identity and wait for its actual result. Applying a profile in the current agent adds no worker. Every new task needs useful contributions from at least two distinct actual workers excluding the coordinator, including Plan, read-only and standalone operations. Product/test/docs changes use an actual Builder and distinct independent Reviewer. Track all substantive authors, including secondary authors and coordinator integration. A coordinator self-check cannot replace either worker's bounded contribution. The coordinator must not perform the assigned child's source work in parallel or silently take over after a failed dispatch. Busy slots mean wait/serialize; unavailable dispatch is an explicit blocker. Keep one implementation owner for overlapping changes and one generator/package owner. Read-only consultations cannot implement. Do not recursively invoke a whole preset from an atomic operation. Resume existing children where supported; otherwise reconcile saved state and actual ownership before replacement. Never assume an unknown executor has stopped. Mandatory delegation applies to the coordinator; already assigned children do not recursively spawn workers or restart the workflow. The coordinator may integrate, package and perform already-authorized publication of the independently accepted result. Selected post-implementation checks run before closure. The coordinator retains final accounting until their results arrive, and the implementation owner repairs authorized findings after any needed plan/review update. Loop uses its stricter manager/reviewer/executor boundary. Continue and report Preserve the original deliverable and dependency groups. Missing access to one dependent action does not authorize substituting a documentation-only result for implementation. Continue useful independent work, retain exact blockers, and reuse settled evidence. Wait for a consultation's finished result before reviewing its dependent plan; do not revise a plan during its critique. Keep the durable checklist synchronized with visible Markdown or an actually supported, acknowledged host checklist surface. Report real changes, observed checks, remaining work and delivered artifacts. Converter output or saved files alone do not prove publication. At task start, check workflow log.py status --project-root <ROOT when a shell is available. Optional debug logging is off by default. When enabled, use its shell wrapper and actual event API; never claim it captured host actions that were not delivered.

resources.title: Composable operations and workflow templates
resources.summary: The default main-skill invocation selects a proportional chain from the actual task, then reads the relevant handlers, profiles and prerequisites. It does not require a full-index evaluation. Explicit standalone choices preserve their boundaries. See automatic selection.
resources.body: Composable operations and workflow templates The default main-skill invocation selects a proportional chain from the actual task, then reads the relevant handlers, profiles and prerequisites. It does not require a full-index evaluation. Explicit standalone choices preserve their boundaries. See automatic selection. A stage completes one narrowly defined operation and writes durable evidence in the existing task record. A complete workflow performs its own end-to-end sequence internally; do not insert that whole workflow as an atomic operation alongside another build chain. Discover (read-only, except the task record) - GRC — Repository Contribution Scout : inventory a cloned repository, inspect its architecture and maintainer priorities, then rank PR-sized contributions by category with source evidence; no code edits, issue creation or PR submission. Use before deciding what to contribute to an unfamiliar upstream project. - GAS — Codebase assessment only : inspect the relevant repository, document existing owners/rules and create an assessment artifact. Does NOT plan/build. Use before planning unfamiliar code. - GRS — Research only : investigate public library/project/implementation options and source evidence; no code changes. Use when technology choices require verified information. - GDA — Design audit : inspect actual UI, design system, component ownership and measured gaps; no UI changes. Use before a redesign. - GAA — Architecture advice : read-only trade-offs/integration boundaries against an existing assessment/plan. Use when system design is a real decision. Plan and review (no application code edits) - GPL — Goal Planner: goals/dependencies/sequence, plan-only, starts a task record. Best for roadmap planning. - GCP — Code Goal Planner: implementation plan grounded in existing source, plan-only, starts a task record. Use when no separate assessment is needed. - GPP — Plan from assessment/design evidence; reuses the record created by GAS/GDA. Use after assessment; avoids repeating discovery. - GDS — Design spec from GDA audit, with components, tokens and responsive behaviours. Use to plan UI without building. - GPR — Independent plan review/critique, fixes R/P/T plan and readiness; no code. Use before execution. Execute (changes tests or production code) - GTF — Write meaningful failing tests only: TDD RED ; intentionally failing feature assertions plus evidence, no application edits. - GEX — Execute existing reviewed plan ; no new plan or record allocation. Use to continue from GPR. - GTE — TDD GREEN executor: consume GTF red tests and current plan review, change product code and rerun checks. Verify (existing implementation; do not implement fixes) - GUT — Run scoped unit/integration/lint/type/build checks. - GVE — End-to-end browser/customer journey verification. - GVR — Independent post-implementation code review. - GVS — Security checks on scoped change. - GVA — Keyboard, focus and responsive accessibility checks. - GVP — Performance budgets and failure recovery measurements. Finish (after implementation) - GVD — Documentation-only updater; reuse doc-updater agent. - GCL — Scoped, behaviour-preserving cleanup (requires test reruns). Complete pipelines (standalone choices or templates for automatic composition) For an explicit pipeline, run that pipeline once. For automatic composition, expand its useful operations, combine complementary stages and deduplicate before executing. Never nest full pipeline commands inside an atomic chain. - G1 Standard: capture → plan → critique → implement/test. - GS Assessed: capture → assess → plan → critique → implement/test. - GA Architecture: capture → architecture consultation → plan → critique → implement/test. - GT Full test-first: capture → plan → critique → TDD agent writes RED, GREEN, refactors/tests in one build. - GB Fast build: reuse/dependency batching and consolidated acceptance under full-scope constraint. Legacy specialized complete workflows ( G6 , G7 , GC , GE , GD , GH etc.) remain supported by their existing G codes and actual handler instructions. The public help surface presents the five primary modes: Auto, Plan, Build, Review and Loop. It is ordinary help, not a custom manual picker. The advanced reference documents all retained commands and their exact dependencies. Do not confuse GVD (docs only) with GD (build + docs) or GVE (E2E verify only) with GE (build + E2E). Use the stage artifact contract, neutral operation catalogue and operation policy for same-record evidence and bounded handoffs. No bundled native queue or public native stage / pipeline runtime is required or supplied.

Category IDs: existing-functionality , new-functionality , bug-fix , performance , reliability , security , testing , documentation , developer-experience , architecture , accessibility , interoperability . resources.title: Project Development Plan Criticizer
resources.summary: Apply the mandatory workflow contract and admission metadata. Record real author/reviewer identities, self versus independent criticism, completed checks, findings/dispositions and exact review bindings. Pending placeholders and outcome flags are insufficient.
resources.body: Project Development Plan Criticizer Apply the mandatory workflow contract and admission metadata. Record real author/reviewer identities, self versus independent criticism, completed checks, findings/dispositions and exact review bindings. Pending placeholders and outcome flags are insufficient. Under task routing, every product/test/docs change has an actual independent critic, including G0/G1/GB. Confirm the concrete mode, source-grounded impact, required actual assignments and completed pre-plan Architect advice when broad/shared effects apply. A read-only approach self-check does not replace either of its two useful actual contributors or a selected independent review. Check every substantive author, including secondary contributions and adopted advice, rather than only the primary owner. Critique and revise the selected task record only. Do not fix application code. Preserve the original goal, previous findings, executed evidence and current user authorization. When explicitly requested with planner/executor, run after planning and before execution, passing the same record path without another process question. Do not start other task/planning workflows. Apply the selected command’s hooks from its command file; see shared execution. Workflow 1. Read record-contract.md and select the exact supplied or preceding record. Always pass the conversation-selected record explicitly to resolve plan record.py --project-root <ROOT --record <RECORD . Multiple active records require context-based resolution or one concise question, not newest-record guessing. 2. Read all six files, applicable project instructions, relevant source/diff and supporting evidence. A plan's assertions are not source proof. For partially implemented work, inspect actual changes; do not infer success from checked boxes. Read the selected sources for this review and relevant retained constraints; independently reconcile in-scope issues against their checkpoints and specific tests. A parent R/P/T match is insufficient when a child commitment has no decisive assertion. Restore omitted checkpoints before admitting execution; copying the whole transcript alone does not establish coverage. 3. Check scope before completeness: first derive the authorized outcomes and constraints from the actual selected conversation, without adopting the plan's requested/necessary labels. Apply the contract's behavioral scope review to every R/P/T change, including added clauses and effects around unchanged components or data. Identify its supporting phrase or test its necessity against evidence and a narrower solution. A whole-message citation, existing R ID or claimed safeguard is not a scope finding. Remove unwarranted additions and restore lost constraints before improving the design. Then investigate source-backed diagnosis, paths, dependencies, conventions, permissions, sequencing/recovery and decisive verification. Also check for under-delivery: an older planning-only instruction must not cancel a later authorized stage 3. Reject changing implementation outcomes into "specify/document future work" unless that is the user's current deliverable. Verify the stages/deliverable/completion evidence in fix-plan.md against the chronological request and any clarification that continued the invocation. Scope protection must not become a reason to remove authorized implementation. 4. Append findings in critique.md with stable F ID, severity, source/requirement, concrete defect and likely impact, affected R/P/T section, smallest correction and disposition: fixed in plan, rejected with reason or unresolved. Substantiate the review with the concrete material behavior changes and their authority, reusing the plan's scope delta where accurate. A blanket "no additions" or "all requirements trace to S1" is insufficient. Resolve conflicts between the narrative, source, plan, diff and results; a ready flag or successful helper cannot override missing or contradictory review evidence. “Fixed in plan” never means application code fixed. 5. Correct checklist.md, fix-plan.md, test-plan.md and metadata mappings, never the preserved source text. Update the short scope delta in fix-plan.md and report added/removed behavior in critique.md (or explicitly none). Each accepted addition must trace to user authority or an evidenced necessary detail. Record rejected/optional findings outside executable mappings; do not let optional work block the original task. Preserve historical findings and dated review rounds. Removing an unrequested expansion or fixing an in-scope defect needs no new approval. If a necessary correction would materially expand authorized scope, keep that decision blocked pending the user; do not silently accept it. 6. Increment planRevision for substantive plan changes. Record critiqueOutcome ready (no material revision), revised (corrections incorporated), or blocked. Set reviewedPlanRevision to the actual reviewed revision only after the final cross-check. 7. Recheck original source → R → P → T in both directions, including unchanged behavior and deferred phases. Account for all material added effects, not just validation or approval mechanisms; check that the critic's own corrections also pass the same scope review. Claims about unchanged files do not settle behavioral scope. For ready/revised, finalize with --stage criticized only after completing the substantive review; pending text, unsupported declarations and unresolved contradictions cannot be finalized as reviewed. For unresolved blockers, retain them and set status criticized, readiness blocked, critiqueOutcome blocked. Reconcile every relevant itemized conversation finding with its checklist checkpoint and disposition. An omitted item, a misleadingly merged item, or an optional suggestion silently promoted into executable work is a scope defect even when all existing R/P/T references are valid. Explicitly reconcile the user's bullets, numbered items, checkboxes and nested children under the record contract's user-list coverage check, including items in the invocation itself. When corrections change the checklist, publish the updated Tasks panel if available and acknowledged; otherwise show the updated Markdown checklist in a progress message. Preserve its actual verification state. 8. If work was executing, do not race an active executor. Coordinate/confirm it has stopped before changing the record. Preserve results and reconcile changed checklist evidence; do not mark unexecuted revised steps complete. Review discipline Prioritise scope, reuse, tests that can detect failure and unsafe side effects. Scale depth to risk; preferences and hypothetical future improvements are nonblocking. After material changes, re-review affected findings rather than reopening settled work without evidence. Keep one critique.md; no numeric self-confidence gate or new approval ceremony. Self-critique is not independent review. Completion Report concrete findings and corrections, rejected points, unresolved blockers, exact record path, and whether the revised plan passes the execution gate. Include or publish the revised checklist when changed; plan corrections do not mark implementation outcomes complete. Do not execute it unless the user also requested execution. Contract and tooling Read record-contract.md before operating. Follow applicable project policy and the current user's scope. Use the authorized available browser only for browser-visible claims; an unavailable preferred browser does not justify claiming visual verification.

resources.body: Optional debug logging Logging is off unless explicitly enabled. It is a local diagnostic trail, not a new task record, test result or approval gate. No service, telemetry upload or background watcher is installed. Requires the existing Python 3.10+ runtime. Enable, inspect or disable Resolve the actual installed skill root as SKILL and project root as ROOT : Configuration is $ROOT/.aidw-debug/config.json ; events are appended to $ROOT/.aidw-debug/events.jsonl . Disabling preserves existing logs. The directory gets its own ignore file; existing repository ignore rules are not rewritten. AIDW LOG=0 overrides enabled configuration for one process; AIDW LOG=1 enables it for a process. Child commands inherit this setting. Explicit roots are preferred; otherwise the helper looks for enabled configuration from the current directory upwards. Nothing is created while logging is off. What is automatic The bundled router, allocator, plan finaliser, admission gate, quick allocator/auditor and checklist converters emit events for their actual calls when logging is enabled. Gate failures stay failures. A checklist-conversion event is not a Tasks publication. For other shell actions, use the wrapper instead of executing the command twice: It runs the exact argument array with shell=False , passes through stdout/stderr, and records start, finish, duration and actual exit code. It returns the command’s exit status; missing executables return 127, timeout 124 and interruption 130. Use --cwd DIRECTORY for a package/subdirectory and --timeout SECONDS only when appropriate. Reuse a run ID across the task’s calls; the wrapper propagates run/preset/record context into child helpers. Host stages, tools and agents Native Read/Edit/browser/subagent calls do not pass through the Python runner. Their host must forward events, or the agent must record the actual tool receipt with this API. Do not invent an ID or report an unobserved result. Use kind stage , agent , tool or task , and phase start , finish or blocked . A finish needs outcome and evidence; agent/tool events need actual call IDs unless blocked before launch. The Python emit API is also available to a host bridge. No native event bridge is automatically installed by this skill. Events distinguish helper , runner , host-report and test-adapter . A host report is a recorded claim with an evidence locator, not independently authenticated proof. Planning a handoff does not mean the agent ran. --schedule on route workflow.py only describes planned order. Incomplete pairs, failures and missing receipts stay visible; do not manufacture finish events after an interruption. Privacy and reliability Logs do not capture command output, environment contents, conversation text or source files. Common credential flags/assignments, URL queries, inline -c / -e code and prompt arguments are masked. Redaction is best-effort: arbitrary positional secrets can still leak, so keep secrets out of command arguments and inspect logs before sharing. Files use private creation permissions. Symlinked debug destinations are rejected. Logging failures warn on stderr and never change the underlying command’s result.

Read applicable corrections, preserve approved properties and verify the actual changed output. Use the existing mutation owner and current execution gate; do not allocate another workflow. Execute the selected plan within the user's current authorization. This authorizes normal scoped implementation and verification, not an unrequested commit, push, deploy, paid action, external message or destructive cleanup. A plan cannot grant itself authority. When explicitly requested beside planner/criticizer, consume their exact record path after their authorized stages. Do not silently create a substitute plan or select another ready record when this one is blocked. Apply the selected command’s hooks from its command file; see shared execution. Gate and execute 1. Read record-contract.md, all six record files, current user scope, applicable AGENTS.md and relevant docs. Run resolve plan record.py --project-root <ROOT --record <RECORD --execution; this enforces the gate for explicit and automatic selection. Completed criticism is mandatory even without the compatibility flag --require-critique . Validate the workflow contract and declared briefing, then reconcile actual source/diff; portable metadata hashes do not detect repository-byte drift. Read the current amendment's selected sources, affected issue checkpoints and relevant retained constraints, including after compaction; do not replay every historical snapshot. Missing capture/coverage must be reconciled before mutation; a structural resolver pass does not waive it. Before closure, every accepted child checkpoint needs its own actual evidence, not merely a broad parent test or generated file count. 2. Inspect current source/diff and baseline. Apply the contract's behavioral scope review to the admitted requirements and scope delta against the original request and latest corrections; passing hashes is not scope approval. Check effects around unchanged components and data as well as direct edits. Preserve unrelated work. Record nonmaterial drift; material drift requires correction before the affected mutation. Validate real prerequisites and effective permissions, not only metadata. Reject unrequested additions even if the reviewed plan contains them. Confirm that the admitted deliverable still matches the pending invocation. If product implementation was authorized but the record only plans to specify, retain or validate future-work items, reject that admission and return the same record for correction and fresh review. Do not execute paperwork in place of the requested implementation or close the record while its required product outcomes remain unchecked. Keep real provider/live-action blockers scoped to dependent work; continue independent authorized local work without pretending the entire deliverable is complete. 3. Update checklist/results incrementally so interruption does not lose the record of what happened. Mirror checkbox changes in the Tasks panel or commentary/progress messages in the same work interval as the durable update. Before starting implementation, publish or show the complete admitted checklist with its existing verified state. Keep later user-list additions visible after reconciliation; a new list item must not disappear into an existing broad summary or be checked solely because the user supplied an [x] mark. When new user instructions arrive, apply SKILL.md's semantic follow-up rules to the same record before implementing affected work. Reconcile actual progress, amend affected requirements/checks and refresh material review; preserve unaffected evidence and pending authorized execution. Do not ignore a change because it lacks workflow keywords or create another record from an earlier 0. Before implementing a newly discovered change, compare its effects with the admitted scope, even if it fits an existing R/P label such as integration, recovery or quality. Follow the contract's material-change/review rules before mutation. Diagnose what would fail without the addition; do not justify it with problems created by optional agent-added work. Remove unsupported proposals and continue scoped implementation. Routine internal fixes within the authorized behavior need no new permission. 5. Run the planned checks with exact evidence, including the affected behavior that must remain unchanged. For an enumerated change, verify exactly that set and the relevant untouched neighbors. Add only narrowly necessary checks prompted by new in-scope findings. Keep investigation and verification separate from new persistent behavior or side effects. Repair in-scope failures and rerun affected checks; retain failed evidence and distinguish partial implementation. Test failures and tool limitations do not authorize unrelated features, workflow changes or wider permissions. 6. If a blocker appears, record reason, completed changes and exact next action; set blocked/readiness blocked. Do not broaden the task or silently replan. 7. On explicit continuation, use the same record. Reconcile actual diff and last attempt before any retry. Resolve blockers using evidence; refresh review if the plan changed. After saving original admission evidence, use finalize plan record.py --record <RECORD --project-root <ROOT --stage criticized --resume as described in the contract, then the resolver with --record and --resume. Do not blindly repeat uncertain external actions or erase previous outcomes. 8. Review changed files, actual effects and final diff against the source-derived scope, including configuration, generated outputs and operations beyond source edits. Explain material before/after behavior and its authority in results.md; reconcile it with the plan and critique. Do not retroactively label an unsupported addition requested or declare no scope change despite contrary evidence. Remove this attempt's unsupported changes where safely separable, preserving unrelated work and prior evidence; resolve inseparable ownership before reversal. Record files, check IDs, commands/procedures, exit codes, outcomes, environment, evidence links and remaining states. Close this record with status complete only when every in-scope requirement and accepted issue checkpoint has decisive evidence and material scope discrepancies are resolved; otherwise blocked. Explicitly report it as done/closed without archiving the conversation or changing another record. Unrequested deployment is not a reason to call a finished code-only task blocked. Completion Return record path, outcomes, changes, actual checks and material limitations. Publish the final checklist state to the Tasks panel when available and acknowledged; otherwise render the complete actual Markdown checklist in the final response: [x] for each decisively verified completed outcome and [ ] for each remaining outcome, with its blocker or verification gap. This is required after partial or interrupted execution as well as successful execution; counts or file links alone do not show which items were completed. Distinguish implemented, tested, browser-verified, committed, pushed, deployed and user-accepted; report relevant unreached states without a generic disclaimer list. The manager records that reviewer's decision without substituting its own product judgment. resources.title: Loop — Execute and Review
resources.summary: Follow the mandatory workflow contract: capture scope, plan and criticize proportionately, announce ordered phases/owners and the actual numeric agent count, and pass current admission before every product write.
resources.body: Loop — Execute and Review Follow the mandatory workflow contract: capture scope, plan and criticize proportionately, announce ordered phases/owners and the actual numeric agent count, and pass current admission before every product write. Use Loop for an authorized review-and-repair loop over existing work. Start with review. The current agent is the manager; a separate reviewer judges the work and a separate executor changes it. The manager reconciles the checklist and coordinates the workers. The Reviewer alone decides substantive acceptance. A clean initial result also needs a distinct Verification Engineer contribution acknowledged by that Reviewer. Continue until the applicable independent review accepts the current result, or an actual blocker, interruption or cancellation prevents progress. Contents 1. Enter and recover the task 2. Own the right work 3. Review the originals and result 4. Build the checklist and admit execution 5. Execute and reconcile 6. Review again and continue 7. Monitor every five minutes 8. Checkpoint and report Enter and recover the task Explicit forms include loop <task and /ai-development-workflow loop <task . In ChatGPT, select the main skill from @ autocomplete and append loop and the task; a compatible local host can use $ai-development-workflow loop <task . XR , /ai-dev-loop and the historical /ai-dev-execute-review remain explicit router aliases, not separately registered public skills. Quoted commands or field names inside ordinary task prose are not invocations. The descriptor is modes/loop.json. Continuation callers use --selected-mode loop alongside an actual retained --selected-preset where present. Legacy --selected-mode XR is accepted. Routing describes the mode; it does not spawn workers, start a timer or allocate a record. The public mode is named Loop. Existing artifacts/xr/ evidence paths and xr- serialized schemas remain unchanged for compatibility. Do not rename old checkpoint bytes, hash chains or wire identifiers merely to make their spelling match the public name. Recover the original request, adopted corrections, source/reference files, latest result, allowed changes and actual target environment. With bare Loop, use the related work already identified in the conversation. Ask only for a genuinely missing target or source that cannot be recovered. A request to add or explain Loop does not itself launch an indefinite repair run. Preserve explicit audit-only, plan-only and no-publish boundaries; resolve an explicit conflicting write-capable invocation instead of silently executing repairs. Reuse the exact active compatible development record. If only a quick G0 checklist or chat/artifact record exists, preserve it as source evidence and announce a one-time promotion: allocate one six-file development record through the existing GAS stage-0 helper, cross-link the records, and carry original request provenance, stable IDs and actual evidence/status. Keep the original request/checklist/history unchanged; copied checkmarks do not grant Loop acceptance. If no record exists, allocate once through the same helper and capture the request. Use that new development record for every later round/resume; never repeatedly promote or launch a second assessment pipeline. Do not pass a quick record to six-file admission. Keep the record's actual workflowPreset and record Loop in additive mode metadata/results. Loop is a public mode using the same record, not a new G preset. Follow the record contract; subsequent rounds never allocate another record. Inventory sources and required targets/states before review. Bind comparisons to actual source/result revisions (commit plus relevant working changes, hashes or provider versions). An original document can specify behavior without providing a runnable original page: record that distinction. Do not invent original interactions or infer visuals from markup alone. Use task contracts to distinguish reconstruction from authorized changes. Own the right work Role Owns Does not own --- --- --- Manager Task context, real dispatch, review-to-checklist mapping, item accounting, timer/status checks, saved state and handoff Product inspection, visual/code quality review, fixes, or acceptance judgments Reviewer with loop-review Original/result investigation, actual interactions, comparison, complete findings, repair-plan confirmation and substantive acceptance Product/source repairs or approving its own implementation Builder with loop-execution The admitted checklist, scoped changes, appropriate tests and item-by-item implementation evidence Deleting findings, weakening criteria, changing scope or declaring independent acceptance Verification Engineer Independent decisive coverage/check corroboration for a clean initial result Repairs, manager accounting or replacing the Reviewer’s acceptance decision Launch actual agents with the complete assigned profile and task-local inputs. Record returned worker IDs; a profile applied in prose is not a spawn. Preserve the host's actual models and tools. If independent workers are unavailable, keep the missing capability explicit and do useful preparation; never present manager self-review as the requested independent loop. For every browser worker, supply the complete browser recovery policy and current session owner. Automatic recovery after an unexpected browser handoff requires explicit permission from the current user for the session and support from the host. Reviewers/executors recover their own assigned browser work; the manager remains a coordinator and does not review the product. Keep reviewer and executor phases sequential. There is one implementation owner at a time. Never start execution while review is still changing its findings. Never start a reviewer against a moving output from an active executor. A timer wake coordinates the existing worker; it does not authorize a duplicate worker or concurrent manager edits. Review the originals and result First launch a reviewer in fresh context with the original request/corrections, unchanged sources, current result, inventory, allowed differences, project rules, record and output paths. Require three explicit report sections: 1. Original: Document the relevant pages/files, structure/content, appearance and behavior. Open the originals and exercise available controls, buttons, links, navigation, tabs/panels, forms, states and document actions. Record what each does and what is unavailable. 2. Current result: Repeat the applicable investigation on the delivered work. Use equivalent viewport, data, theme, font, selected state and timing where meaningful. Check the actual latest output and its complete required target set, including hidden and below-fold content. 3. Comparison and findings: Record structural, visual and functional differences; missing content/features; broken/incomplete actions; mistakes; regressions; and concrete improvements. Distinguish permitted differences, confirmed defects, uncertainty and optional proposals. Each finding needs a stable ID, affected target/state, source requirement, observation and evidence, impact, smallest scoped correction, preserved properties and acceptance check. Keep all findings in the report. Severity orders work; it does not erase minor requested work. Optional unrelated improvements remain documented proposals, not hidden executable scope. Missing access is an unresolved coverage item, never a passed check. For UI, give the reviewer the UI Design Director, applicable corrections and visual review instructions. Require real rendering and interaction for those claims; source/build checks prove narrower things. For documents, use the actual document format/runtime where applicable. Inspect all requested targets; a contact sheet or sample is not exhaustive evidence. Reuse domain owners instead of inventing tools. Build the checklist and admit execution Wait for the completed review artifact and actual worker result. The manager converts every in-scope actionable finding into stable, source-linked checklist items with acceptance criteria, dependencies, allowed files/targets and evidence requirements. Preserve the finding-to-item map; split independent commitments so a broad checkbox cannot hide unfinished work. Link duplicates explicitly. Retain blocked and out-of-scope dispositions with their reasons; do not silently discard an item, narrow the target inventory or replace a failed criterion with an easier one. Use the existing checklist.md , fix-plan.md , test-plan.md and R/P/T mappings. Save round evidence under artifacts/xr/ using Loop artifacts. Show the visible checklist in ordinary Markdown, or use an actually supported and acknowledged host checklist surface. The manager transcribes and reconciles these artifacts; it does not independently inspect the product. The initial report cannot approve an arbitrary plan written later. Pass the exact derived checklist/plan revision back to that reviewer for substantive confirmation of fidelity, feasibility, scope and decisive checks. Use the reviewer's actual response in critique.md . Reuse an earlier independent critique only if its exact plan and relevant source remain current. Material changes require reviewer confirmation again. This is part of the review phase, not another user-permission round or manager quality review. Finalize the reviewed record and apply resolve plan record.py --execution --require-critique with its explicit record path; use the documented resume gate after reconciling interruption. Do not manufacture readiness. Execute and reconcile After the reviewer-confirmed handoff, spawn the executor. Provide the original request, review report, entire admitted checklist, plan/critique revision, current baseline, protected properties, expected tests, output paths and assigned write scope. The executor works through every item, records actual changes/tests, and reports each ID as implemented, blocked or not run with the matching evidence and output revision. It must return a partial/blocked report when unable to finish. A statement that everything is done cannot replace the item accounting. On return, the manager checks the checklist only : exact IDs, complete coverage, statuses, dependencies, required evidence references, revision bindings and unresolved items. The bookkeeping helper can detect structural omissions; it does not judge whether the fix works or authenticate a claim. Missing accounting goes back to the executor. An actual blocker remains visible; continue independent authorized work where useful. Do not mark independently verified completion from the executor's claim. Use an explicit implemented-awaiting-review state in the round evidence and keep final completion unresolved. The manager must not open the app, inspect the diff or rerun product checks to decide quality. Those are reviewer duties. The executor may not change the checklist's requirements or its verification criteria just to obtain a pass. Necessary new scope is recorded for proper review. Review again and continue When all checklist items have complete implementation accounting and the executor has stopped, spawn a new reviewer with a new identity and fresh context . Give it the original sources, latest instructions, exact new result revision, expected inventory and prior finding IDs. Include execution evidence as claims to investigate, not proof to trust. Have it repeat the original/result comparison and relevant interactions, verify each fix, and look for omissions and regressions outside the executor's reported list. Missing independent-worker support blocks the independent loop; useful preparation may continue, but manager role-play cannot replace it. XR remains an invocation alias. Legacy xr- schemas and checkpoint paths remain unchanged so earlier evidence and hash chains can be read truthfully. It preserves literal text such as “Go through these files”, “3 columns” and “Plan only” as prose; semantic scope still governs the selected work. Use --text only when the caller has identified an explicit control. Router output describes the route; it does not execute phases or launch workers. menu and --menu request a small ordinary help response containing the five primary modes and a link to advanced documentation. The package supplies no editor popup, model picker, native queue or custom ChatGPT UI. Native stage <id and pipeline <id selectors are retired; report that boundary rather than falling through to a write-capable route. Continuation and conflicts Continue the same record and reconcile the latest request, source, worker status and evidence. Retain the selected mode when it is still applicable; a planning-only continuation stays planning-only. A new explicit implementation request can move the same work into Build or Loop after current review. Corrections reopen affected outcomes and preserve prior history. Current explicit boundaries prevail. A conflicting request such as “loop, but do not change anything” needs its intent resolved; never use the mode name to erase the boundary. Ask only for a material unresolved decision or missing source that available context cannot supply.
