resources.body: Shared record contract (revision 2) Apply the mandatory workflow contract and admission metadata. Every execution/resume requires current completed criticism and a declared public briefing; no preset or omitted flag waives them. All stages share the bundled plan record.py and finalize plan record.py. They have no third-party dependencies or sibling-skill imports. Use Python 3.10 or newer. The six-file development record lives under documents/tasks/development and contains record.json, checklist.md, fix-plan.md, test-plan.md, critique.md and results.md. Planning, criticism and execution share that directory. For explicit legacy numeric workflows, only stage 0 creates a record; without 0 they reuse the selected existing one. Public Auto/Plan/Build/Review/Loop can capture a fresh task once through the existing allocator as their contracts specify, or reuse the selected compatible record. They do not require the user to type a creation digit. Do not create duplicate records for operations or erase earlier results. Necessary evidence files may be added. Automatic composition with real workers An automatic chain follows task routing, resolves a concrete mode, assigns meaningful work to actual workers and uses the existing record and source/readiness gates. Allocate at most once using an existing starter; later operations reuse that record. Store selection and continuation in artifacts/workflow-selection.json and results.md , as described in automatic selection. Keep the real starter in workflowPreset ; do not introduce an AUTO preset. Completed stage evidence is reused only after source and plan-revision reconciliation. The selection validator does not replace this contract, dispatch workers or authenticate evidence. Loop mode Loop reuses the selected six-file record and keeps its actual workflowPreset. With no compatible development record, invoke the existing GAS stage-0 allocation once. If the selected work has only a quick G0 or chat/artifact record, explicitly preserve that original, cross-link the one new development record and carry request provenance, stable IDs and real evidence/status. Keep the old record kind/content; do not infer acceptance from copying checkmarks. All later Loop rounds reuse the new record. This narrow Loop promotion does not change normal G0 behavior, replace the record schema or start a second assessment pipeline. Record Loop mode/run/round checkpoints as additive artifacts. The manager derives and reconciles the checklist, the reviewer confirms the exact current repair-plan revision, and the executor passes the existing critique gate. Executor-reported implementation remains awaiting fresh reviewer acceptance. Manager accounting is not substantive review, and a timer wake neither approves work nor creates another record. Public-mode capture and internal operations Public modes capture or reuse one task record. The coordinator calls the existing allocator only for a genuinely fresh selected task; internal operations and workers reuse that exact result. A standalone G starter retains its original allocation semantics. An explicitly unavailable record path is a blocker, not permission to choose another record. There is no native queue record exception in this edition. Retain historical records as evidence without pretending their unavailable host integration ran. Loop preserves its old artifacts/xr/ paths and xr- serialized schemas for checkpoint compatibility; the public mode name is loop . An old checkpoint must be reconciled with actual current worker state. Metadata Retain schema project-development-plan/v1 for identification; contractVersion: 2 adds execution gating. projectRoot is the verified absolute local project root; recordPath is relative to it. Remote-only source analysis must remain not ready until rebound to a verified checkout; never set a repository URL as an executable projectRoot. status: draft planned criticized executing blocked complete. readiness: not ready ready blocked. blockers: [] only when no unresolved implementation decision or verification prerequisite remains. critiqueOutcome: not requested ready revised blocked. planRevision: positive integer; increment on scope, change sequence, verification or material plan edits. reviewedPlanRevision: revision covered by the latest completed critique. sourceBaseline: description plus revision/dirtyPaths when Git exists; for a non-Git project record exact relevant file evidence. This is not an automatic Git cleanliness requirement. scope: in/out arrays of concrete boundaries. requestSources: append-only objects with id, role (user/context/policy), origin (message locator or descriptive conversation reference; policy path/section), and verbatim text. requestHashes: per-source SHA-256 stamped by the finalizer. Keep prior hashes; append new sources, never reseal edited history. requirements: objects with id, text, sources (source IDs), and kind (requested/necessary). Necessary items also require justification: evidence and why the requested outcome cannot be correctly achieved without this detail. steps: objects with id, requirements (IDs), paths, change, dependsOn (step IDs). checks: objects with id, requirements (IDs), method, expected, boundary. planHashes: SHA-256 of checklist.md, fix-plan.md and test-plan.md at readiness review. definitionHash: SHA-256 of normalized root/path, revision, source baseline, scope, request provenance and R/P/T mappings. Metadata edits also invalidate readiness. critiqueHash: SHA-256 of critique.md when a critique is completed. Preserve createdAt; update updatedAt with timezone-aware UTC. Keep metadata concise; put detailed evidence and commands in Markdown. IDs connect metadata to corresponding Markdown sections. A syntactically valid record does not prove the plan is sensible, source is current, tests passed, or the user authorized execution. Request authority Before plan derivation, capture the selected messages under source capture, with their original locators. Preserve historical sources; capture only new substantive amendment sources and reuse unchanged sources. Identify current amendment sources in fix-plan.md; historical retention does not require rereading all archives. Keep one checkpoint per distinct in-scope issue with decisive assertions, not a row for incidental discussion. See source capture for sensitivity, verification and missing-history handling. The six core files and existing metadata schema remain; conversation snapshots are source evidence, not a replacement task record. Hash equality proves capture fidelity only, not semantic coverage. For a time-anchored invocation, record the resolved inclusive conversation range in fix-plan.md (start date/time/timezone and start/end message locators). Preserve the invocation and scoped source text in requestSources with actual roles. Multiple matching times select the most recent matching message through the invocation, after explicit selectors; they do not require clarification. Resolve genuinely unavailable boundaries and missing range content before record mutation. Earlier context preserves constraints but adds work only when explicitly adopted; later corrections append sources and do not rewrite the original boundary. See timestamp matching. This uses existing files and fields, not a new schema or a machine-enforced timestamp parser. Preserve the complete relevant user messages and later corrections verbatim in requestSources, including negative constraints, uncertainty, named lists, "only", "first" and "later". A bare invocation selects the underlying related request, not a new task about creating paperwork. Include only relevant conversation context; label assistant explanations context, never user authorization. If an existing authoritative request.md already contains the text, reuse its source IDs/locators when recording the text here; do not create another source document. After first finalization, sources are append-only. Append corrections with new IDs and identify what they supersede in the plan; retain the old text and hashes. Do not edit or clear old requestHashes to make a changed request pass. The helper detects accidental source changes during normal finalization, not malicious rewriting of both text and hashes, and cannot determine whether a quote or justification is truthful. Compare against the actual conversation at review and execution. Each R item must be requested (citing a user source) or necessary (citing user/policy authority and evidence-backed justification). A necessary detail may preserve existing behavior, fulfill an actual dependency or satisfy mandatory safety policy; it cannot choose an optional product feature. Source references prove provenance exists, not that the requirement follows from it. Check both directions: every requested outcome/constraint is covered, and every executable item is warranted. Keep optional proposals outside executable R/P/T mappings. User-list coverage Before deriving or revising the checklist, enumerate the individual items in the selected user's bullets, numbered lists, Markdown checklists, nested lists, and itemized table rows, including lists in the invocation and later amendments. Read surrounding prose and parent items with each child so that conditions, exclusions, sequence, and acceptance details remain attached. Preserve the original list text and checkbox marks in the existing source archive/requestSources; a formatted message is still a source request. Give each distinct requested outcome or constraint its own source-linked R checkpoint and corresponding checklist checkbox. Split an item with multiple independent commitments when a single checkbox could hide unfinished work. Keep grouping labels as context rather than creating artificial action items. Shared implementation steps or tests do not erase individual outcomes. Reuse stable IDs for duplicates/corrections and retain all relevant source mappings; do not collapse an entire list into "address all requested changes." Before finalizing planning and during criticism, compare every source-list item against the checklist. Each must be covered or explicitly accounted for as duplicate, non-actionable context, out of scope, deferred, superseded, or already verified, with a reason when plausible requested work is excluded. Explicitly requested items are in scope unless actual authority says otherwise; the agent's preference is not an exclusion reason. Hypothetical suggestions and assistant findings retain their existing authority boundaries. A user-supplied [x] alone does not verify the item in the current execution. For example, a message asking to show the checklist while building it, show checked-off items after execution, and include items from user lists contains three distinct commitments. Preserve all three as separate checkpoints rather than one "improve checklist handling" row. Visible checklist and execution reporting The durable checklist.md and user-visible list contain the same stable IDs, scope and state. Show the initial draft while planning is underway, material additions/corrections, current progress and final reconciled outcomes in ordinary Markdown. Label partial drafts and include the durable record path. A promise or file link alone is not visible checklist publication. An actually available host checklist/plan tool may mirror the list through its documented schema and returned acknowledgment. This package does not install a custom panel or define that host API. Do not report a panel updated from a local converter or an attempted call. If a supported visible surface is unavailable, failed or incomplete, use the complete Markdown list; do not omit items because a tool has size or state limits. Use the record directory name as a stable list identity and retain R IDs on every update. Keep unresolved items visible. Replace a list only to reconcile its complete intended state; never erase unfinished work through omission. Mark complete only after decis

resources.summary: Follow the mandatory workflow contract: capture scope, plan and criticize proportionately, announce ordered phases/owners and the actual numeric agent count, and pass current admission before every product write.
resources.body: Shared contract for environment specialists Follow the mandatory workflow contract: capture scope, plan and criticize proportionately, announce ordered phases/owners and the actual numeric agent count, and pass current admission before every product write. For visual outcomes, combine the UI Design Director under UI applicability. Use it for visual judgment and correction coverage while the native kit, platform and format specialist retains its actual implementation contract. This is required expertise within existing operations, not an additional writer or scope expansion. Follow progress announcements: name workflow, stage and responsible role before work and each transition; distinguish current-chat profiles from successfully launched agents. A specialist is a concrete domain profile assigned to an existing workflow operation. Select it from inspected source and task needs. It does not create another workflow, grant permissions, select a model, register a native agent or install a new dependency. The coordinator follows task routing and delegates every task to actual workers. Already assigned children perform that bounded operation without recursively spawning. Six canonical worker families own work; the existing 21 lenses supply domain knowledge. A new task requires at least two useful actual contributors, not one worker per lens. Include every substantive author in independence checks and record each result’s limitations and effect on synthesis. Before specialist assignment, search the packaged resource index from the request and refine it with inspected project evidence when needed. Review grouped candidates and their use/avoid matches. For a selected recipe, select or give a task-specific non-applicability reason for each recommended lens. Read chosen profiles completely and pass their full instructions—not only an ID—to the assigned worker. Record the path, concrete question, acceptance criteria, inspected evidence and effect on synthesis. Provenance cannot prove comprehension; independent review checks the result. Assignment Pass the selected profile in full to an actual assigned agent, together with: - The original request, corrections, requirements and in/out scope. - Source checkout/root, relevant baseline, installed versions and intended runtime. - The exact existing task record and consumed evidence paths. - The chosen operation: assess, research, plan, implement, review or verify. - Allowed files, write boundary, expected artifact and acceptance criteria. - Other active owners and any existing specialist plugin that governs the deliverable. - For browser work, the browser recovery policy, the current session owner, and any explicit session-specific permission from the current user. Pause on handoff by default. Without an implementation assignment the specialist is read-only apart from its task artifact. During implementation it follows the current reviewed plan and has only the assigned source ownership. The same agent must not claim independent review of its own work. Do not spawn one worker per specialist lens: combine compatible lenses in actual scoped assignments. Keep the mandatory execution/independent-review separation for writing work, and the actual meaningful specialist assignment for read-only work. Concrete work and evidence Identify real entry points, canonical owners, contracts and environment versions before applying advice. Trace behaviour through the actual system. Return file/symbol references, confirmed findings, uncertainty, implementation boundaries and relevant checks. Preserve user-approved content, design tokens, existing data and unrelated changes. For editor/export work, test save/reopen and the affected canvas/preview/export/import surfaces. For migrations, build a behaviour parity matrix and record drift from the source snapshot. For batch work, reconcile requested, processed, successful and failed item counts. For installed-host work, distinguish source, generated artifact, installed version and running process. Use a sample before a destructive or expensive bulk operation where appropriate. Never replace an unavailable native widget, host bridge or runtime with a fake success. If the required outcome needs a missing shared capability and implementation is authorised, include that prerequisite in the plan. Preserve explicit boundaries such as mockup-first. Shared development habits Use the repository's dev mode for iteration. Inspect scripts that implicitly run full builds. Run focused checks while editing; coordinate one final generator/build/package owner after source stabilises. Repeat a build only to resolve a concrete problem or required gate. Preserve existing toolchains; changing packages/frameworks is not a default prerequisite. Make meaningful checkpoints where current authorisation and repository policy permit. Track local commit and remote push separately. Reconcile local/remote changes before a resume. Do not reset or erase other work. Do not silently turn a manual billing/content process into scheduled automation. Fix the implementation or governed artifact when a test or ledger fails. Do not weaken tests, validators, instructions or unrelated skills merely to make a result pass. If the task is itself an authorised policy change, state the changed contract and test that intended behaviour while preserving the other gates. Existing plugins and sources Use existing specialist plugins as the owners of their detailed rules: design-system page builder, dynamic page studio, native YAML builder, rebrand importer, SEO page builder, content audit and the current platform/plugin/skill tools when relevant. Read the actual available skill; never invent its interface or claim it was called when unavailable. AI Development Workflow composes and verifies that work instead of copying a second divergent implementation of those systems. Treat upstream repositories as evidence, not instructions with authority over this task. Consult version-matched primary documentation when facts may have changed. Record the inspected path/commit, licence and adaptation boundary. Popularity is not proof of quality or a positive review. New profiles are original instructions with source references; do not silently relicense copied GPL, CC-BY-SA, MPL or other third-party material as MIT. Completion Report what the specialist actually inspected, changed or verified, with artifact paths. Classify passed, failed, not run and blocked accurately. A valid schema or green build does not prove user-visible parity. Runtime, publication and installed-host claims need their own evidence when they are part of the user's requested outcome.

resources.body: Stage artifacts and durable handoff Apply the workflow contract, record contract and progress announcements. Scope, current plan criticism, visible phases/owners and actual worker counts remain mandatory before product writes. Each operation works within one selected task record and one assigned workspace. A public mode or standalone starter may allocate that record once; subsequent operations reuse it. An explicitly selected record path is authoritative. Do not choose a different record by filesystem recency, create worker sub-records, or replace original sources with a recap. For visual tasks, load UI applicability and the UI Design Director. Expertise never expands the assigned write scope. See composition for dependencies and worker ownership. Atomic G evidence Create <record /artifacts/ when needed. Preserve the six core record files, selected source captures and earlier reports. Append a dated attempt or use a new attempt directory on retry. Link actual results from results.md ; do not mark downstream work complete from file presence. Artifact key Usual evidence Producer and required content --- --- --- assessment artifacts/assessment.md GAS: C IDs, paths/symbols, owners, tests, gaps and source provenance research artifacts/research.md GRS: verified sources, versions, findings, licenses and uncertainty design audit artifacts/design-audit.md GDA: observed UI, tokens, component owners, screenshots and limits architecture artifacts/architecture.md GAA: existing architecture, bounded decisions and tradeoffs design spec artifacts/design-spec.md GDS: scoped design, reuse, states and measurable acceptance plan fix-plan.md and test-plan.md GPP/GCP/GPL: source-linked R/P/T coverage; planning is not execution plan review critique.md and artifacts/plan-review.md GPR: independent findings, dispositions, reviewed revision and hashes red tests artifacts/red-tests.md GTF: actual test files and the correct intentional RED failure implementation artifacts/implementation.md and results.md GEX/GTE: scoped changes and actual verification outcomes unit verification artifacts/unit-verification.md GUT: actual commands, exits, failures and coverage limits e2e verification artifacts/e2e-verification.md GVE: observed journeys, assertions and browser evidence code review artifacts/code-review.md GVR: independent source/diff findings and evidence security verification artifacts/security-verification.md GVS: bounded checks and supported findings accessibility verification artifacts/accessibility-verification.md GVA: semantics, controls, focus and relevant interaction evidence performance verification artifacts/performance-verification.md GVP: named baselines, workloads, measurements and budgets documentation artifacts/documentation.md GVD: changed docs grounded in actual behavior cleanup artifacts/cleanup.md GCL: bounded refactor and affected checks contribution.portfolio Contribution reports and portfolio.json GRC: inventoried repository, source-grounded candidates and validation Internal operations under workflows/ use their own exact artifact keys, such as code.plan and plan.review . The catalogue explicitly normalizes the shipped G artifact aliases for composition; this does not create, inspect or approve the actual evidence. Read the selected instruction and real input before consuming it. Evidence and completion Record the request/requirement, source version, exact output path, actual author/reviewer identity where available, checks performed, observed results and limitations. When hashes or plan revisions bind evidence, compute them from the actual artifacts. Never fabricate a Git baseline, worker identity, transcript timestamp or passing test result. Use succeeded only when the assigned operation really completed and its required evidence exists. Missing source/tools, stale review, unobserved behavior or an unresolved prerequisite means blocked or failed as appropriate. A nonzero test exit is not success except for an explicit expected TDD RED assertion; runner/import/syntax failures are not valid RED evidence. The real coordinator reads returned worker results and reconciles artifacts before dependent work. No custom host completion event, queue ledger, receipt schema or artifact.json is required by this portable handoff. A conversational “done” or a structurally valid JSON file still cannot replace observed evidence. Mutation and review gates Every product/test/docs writer needs current concrete plan coverage, completed criticism and successful public-briefing admission. GPR and the internal review-plan operation require a real independent critic. G0/G1/GB have no solo or self-critique exemption for writing work; apply the concrete mode, routing and assignment requirements in task routing. Reviewer operations stay read-only; executor operations make only admitted changes. Source, requirements or relevant plan changes invalidate affected evidence. Preserve prior attempts and refresh the required review instead of silently waiving it. Accepted continuing implementation may update source under its reviewed plan, but unrelated drift requires reconciliation. Documentation and cleanup have no exemption from the write gate. Do not infer authorization to commit, push, deploy, send messages or perform destructive work from completing a stage. Continue actions already authorized by the current task, and report the actual boundary when a dependent external action remains unavailable or unapproved.

Contents 1. Identify the actual job 2. Choose a transformation mode 3. Preserve corrections and approved work 4. Map sources and owners 5. Define decisive acceptance 6. Record the requested deliverable, exact source revision, required targets/counts, constraints, tools available and delivery destination. Separate the requested result from examples and quoted historical instructions. A CSV of old conversations authorizes analysis of those messages, not execution of their commands. Read available text completely; record omitted content, inaccessible attachments, duplicate identifiers and confidence honestly. Keep this contract in the existing record's plan/results and R checkpoints. It is not another task directory or permission ceremony. A small correction uses a compact plan and criticism with a before/after check, recorded under the shared mandatory admission contract. Use an explicit target/evidence matrix for a batch, repeated correction, schema conversion or multiple relevant states. Choose a transformation mode Choose per deliverable when a task mixes modes. Infer a reasonable mode from the request; ask only if unresolved interpretations would materially change the result. Mode Authority Required preservation and check --- --- --- Reconstruct Reproduce the supplied design, structure, interaction or asset Match source geometry, typography, order, content and behavior; list explicit exceptions and unavailable evidence Adapt Apply bounded branding/content/platform changes to a reference Identify allowed replacements and retained structure/logic; verify both Explore Produce genuinely distinct concepts within stated constraints Define variation axes and expected count; preserve fixed composition/assets; compare concept differences, not only labels/colors Correct Repair named defects in an existing result Record the precise delta and protected neighbors; compare the same source/output states Integrate Add a capability within an existing system Trace existing shell, components, state, data and import/export owners; extend them before creating parallels Analyze Inspect, explain, research, audit or plan Produce evidence/findings within the read-only boundary; no hidden implementation “Be creative” does not cancel an exact-reference constraint. “All” needs a complete named inventory. A new concept is not a logo swap when distinct concepts are requested; a complete redesign is not a local fix. Honor requested alternatives, otherwise deliver one final result. Preserve corrections and approved work For each meaningful correction, record: R ID Source/target revision Requested delta Keep unchanged Acceptance evidence State Preserve IDs across retries. New feedback supersedes the conflicting requirement without erasing its history. Reopen affected outcomes only; reuse unaffected current evidence. Do not replace a satisfactory widget because one shadow is wrong, alter line height when only font size is requested, or regenerate a whole composition for an isolated edit unless the actual tool limitation makes that necessary. Explain material approximation honestly. Before returning a repair, verify the reported defect is observably changed and the protected properties remain. For repeated dissatisfaction, compare against the actual supplied baseline, reproduce the remaining mismatch and diagnose its owner; do not repeat an unchanged output or replace evidence with a higher self-awarded score. Map sources and owners Use a compact source map: source ID version/path role owner coverage/limitations . Latest explicit instructions govern; approved source components, current kits and actual project configuration then establish the implementation. Old examples are subordinate to current corrections. A saved package, generated output, installed plugin and running host can be different revisions; identify which one is being inspected. For supplied ZIP/HTML bundles, inventory all relevant pages, assets, fonts, scripts, variants, screenshots and metadata before implementation. Preserve the baseline. Inspect safe archive paths and counts; do not execute arbitrary scripts merely because they are bundled. For shared UI, map each requested section/control to its canonical component and caller set. Inspect the real API and all relevant options before recreating it. For a native editor, read the current kit, schema, widget registry, examples and rendering contract. Produce a section-to-widget mapping and explicit custom-code exception list. Card slots, product/tabs widgets, presets and nested children must be considered before invented containers or HTML. If the user allows custom HTML only for a map, that exception applies only to that map. Do not generalize a task-specific exception or apply one company's tokens to another project. Keep authorized project preferences in named scoped profiles, beneath current approved project sources. Delegate detailed format rules to the available owner skill: design-system builder, dynamic page studio, native YAML builder, rebrand importer, SEO/content workflow, image-generation tool, browser/runtime tool, or platform/plugin maintenance skill. Read it; do not invent its interface. The workflow coordinates dependencies and acceptance rather than maintaining a competing schema or theme system. If a required tool is absent, finish independent work and state the exact unverified outcome. Define decisive acceptance Work Evidence that resolves the actual risk --- --- Visual reconstruction/correction Matched source/result viewport, data, theme and font state; full-page/section/crop comparison; actual fixed delta and protected neighbors Shared tokens/typography Loaded font/computed styles and explicit mode/accent/font/component/state coverage; inspect nested headers, footers, cards, active controls and maps Animation/interactive widget Observe a full cycle and transitions, timing, reset/pause/speed controls if present, stable geometry, hidden-view behavior and reduced-motion handling where relevant Native YAML Widget capability mapping, schema validation, actual import/edit/save/reopen/export when available, and rendered comparison; syntax alone is not parity Product image set Original asset identity, angle, baseline, placement, scale, spacing, transparency and output dimensions/count; inspect every requested variant Media library integration Existing navigation/tree/drop lifecycle, folder identity and collision behavior, persistent metadata/favorites, automatic conversion if requested, actual preview and export fidelity Content/SEO Current source facts, approved copy, complete page/link inventory, canonical/metadata/schema agreement; no invented services or destinations Distribution/delivery Exact final artifacts/revisions, complete assets/fonts, clean opening/import, actual destination readback or host receipt, requested target count Choose checks by failure risk; do not claim exhaustive state combinations from a sample. Enumerate requested states, identify representative coverage and mark remaining cases unverified. Include responsive/keyboard/focus checks when the affected behavior requires them. Animation screenshots, successful builds and valid YAML each prove a narrower claim. Use acceptance evidence for a machine-checked matrix where useful. No local validator can infer the original visual target or authenticate a provider receipt. Continue and deliver On “continue”, “still wrong”, or a new correction, inspect the active record and actual latest files/repository state. Preserve authorized milestones, avoid rebuilding completed targets, and leave exact next steps after an interruption. Do not use the latest filename alone as proof that the user is viewing the current version. Verify relevant output and destination. Report prepared, generated, tested, visually inspected, saved, pushed, deployed and user- accepted as separate states where relevant. A check needs the exact output revision it observed. Never claim acceptance for the user. Do not let an unavailable upload/deploy step block authorized independent implementation, or describe that unavailable step as completed.

resources.body: Task-specific composition guide Read the relevant workflow entries, selected handlers and their actual dependencies. These are recommendations for composing a proportional chain, not keyword routing rules or commands to run blindly. Keep existing evidence and user scope authoritative. Here “diagnose”, “behaviour”, “visual review”, “goal verify” and “dependency review” refer to bounded internal operations in the neutral catalogue and composition guide. First apply task routing: resolve the concrete mode, delegate actual work, use GB/Fast Engineer for known localized builds, and obtain Architect advice before the final plan for broad/shared effects. These rules take precedence over abbreviated examples below. Portable task recipes The portable recipe catalogue supplies explicit reusable patterns for the work below. Automatic selection loads a relevant recipe and its operation/profile dependencies when the actual task needs them; unrelated entries need no evaluation. The user does not need to choose a code. /ai-development-workflow recipe <id describes a portable chain without dispatching workers. Read task contracts and preserve the current user's scope when adapting it. Automatic selection first searches the packaged resource index, provisionally from the request and then with inspected project evidence when needed. A returned recipe is a candidate, not a decision. If selected, each recommended lens receives a focused selected or not-applicable disposition and every chosen instruction body is read and assigned concretely. Recipe ID Use it for Decisive addition to the existing workflow --- --- --- reference-rebuild Supplied screenshot, HTML, extracted ZIP or approved page Source inventory, protected composition, real component reuse, matched render comparison visual-correction Named defects or repeated dissatisfaction with existing output Exact delta ledger, protected neighbors, current baseline, observable before/after result design-system-rollout Shared components, font sets, modes, accents and presets Canonical token/component owner and explicit nested-state/caller coverage native-yaml-conversion HTML/design to editable native YAML Current kit and widget capability map, card/product/tab composition, explicit code exceptions, real round trip asset-production Product image edits, compositions and constrained variant sets Reference identity, angle/baseline/spacing constraints, allowed variation axes, every output inspected motion-reconstruction Animated heroes, demos, tabs and interactive widgets Actual source logic, sequence and complete-cycle timing/transition evidence media-library-extension New media/icon workflows inside an existing application Shared navigation/tree/drop/state owners, metadata/persistence, conversion fidelity and privacy content-site-delivery Source-grounded pages, content migrations and SEO implementation Current facts and content inventory, approved shared sections, valid links/schema, rendered deliverables artifact-handoff Complete files, imports, packages, destinations and release mismatch Final revision and asset closure, actual destination readback, separate preparation/delivery states plugin-evolution Improve plugins/skills from actual usage or defects Complete evidence coverage, deduplication, sanitized behavior cases, compatible saved release Do not stack two complete recipes. Borrow their useful atomic operations once, retain the review dependency, and combine specialist lenses within real assignments. Small corrections keep an explicitly selected G0 record while using the required Fast Engineer and reviewers; ordinary localized Auto builds use GB. Review-only tasks stay read-only; a missing renderer is an evidence limit, not permission to invent results. Recipes do not supersede a companion plugin's native schema, theme/preset, importer or image-tool contract. General composition patterns Task and evidence Start with Compose the remaining useful operations Domain specialists and decisive evidence --- --- --- --- Small, well-understood reversible fix Inspect actual owner/consumers; GB/Fast Engineer (preserve an explicit G0 record) Compact plan → independent critique → actual execution worker → focused check → independent result review Relevant lens; actual changed behaviour; no solo exemption Unfamiliar substantial build GAS; GRS for uncertain technical choices GPP → GPR → GEX → GUT → GVR; goal verify and GVD when material Stack-matched specialists; requested end-to-end outcomes Bug, regression or silent failure GAS + diagnose GPP → GPR → GTF/GTE when a meaningful regression test fits, otherwise GEX → affected verification → GVR Version/runtime identity, reproduced cause and repaired path React UI or application state GAS; GDA when rendered UI is involved GDS if design changes → GPP → GPR → GEX → GUT/GVE → GVA/visual review as relevant React; editor/schema for persisted editor models; interaction and state parity Editable page/widget/import/export defect GAS + diagnose + existing schema inventory GDA/GDS if visual contract changes → GPP → GPR → GEX → round-trip/output verification → GVR Editor/schema + native YAML/archive; canonical registry, nested content and unknown fields preserved Source-faithful website or screenshot reconstruction Full source/asset inventory + GDA GDS → GPP → GPR → GEX → GVE → visual review → GVA Native YAML/archive + browser extraction as needed; use existing page-builder/importer owners WordPress/WooCommerce feature or issue GAS + installed WP/PHP/plugin versions Diagnose for bug → GPP → GPR → GEX → GUT/GVE → scoped GVS WP/Woo; hooks, capabilities/nonces, data preservation and actual supported runtime WHMCS, billing or external invoice integration GAS + API/data/security contract GRS for current docs → GPP → GPR → GEX → integration tests → GVS → GVR WHMCS + data/database as needed; tenant/account separation, idempotency, pagination and manual-flow preservation AI plugin, skill or MCP update GAS + catalogue/tool/packaging inventory + GRS GAA when integration changes → GPP → GPR → GEX → routing/schema tests → GVR; dependency review if sources change → GVD Plugins/MCP; stable identity, permissions, explicit routing and saved release readback Browser extension, extraction or download issue Installed reproduction + GAS + diagnose GPP → GPR → GEX → browser/storage/ZIP verification → GVR Browser extraction + migration/release; selected/captured/exported counts, assets, interactions and interrupted-download recovery Help centre, Markdown/MDX or content migration Source/status/route inventory + GAS GPP → GPR → GEX → parser/schema/link/route checks → rendered samples → goal verify Content/SEO + native YAML/archive if relevant; exact counts, seo.yaml/schema.yaml and approved copy Python/API pipeline, importer or automation Real input and contract inventory + GAS GRS only for unknown APIs → GPP → GPR → GEX → pagination/retry/idempotency/checkpoint tests → GVR Python/data; partial failures, dedupe keys, missing IDs and reconciled output counts SQL schema or database migration GAS + engine/version/data ownership Required Architect advice → GPP → GPR → reviewed migration → GUT + scoped GVS/GVP Database;
