preserve uncommitted work and don't equate merge with publication Realtime chat/video, dictation or local/native runtime Runtime/lifecycle identity + diagnose GAA only for actual boundary changes → GPP → GPR → GEX → lifecycle/retry/media verification → GVP as relevant Realtime/native; reconnect, cancellation, device/permission changes, persisted recovery and observable readiness Assessment, research, planning or review only Relevant GAS/GRS/GRC/GDA/GAA or explicit stage Stop at requested boundary; planning can include GPP/GPR; review may include GVR/GVS/GVA/GVP No implementation, deployment or hidden fix stage Documentation-only update Existing code/diff and GVD Verify documentation against actual source/commands Content/SEO only if its artefacts are affected; no code rebuild by default Combination examples - A React help-centre migration can combine assessed-build, behaviour-parity and content verification: GAS → behaviour → GPP → GPR → GEX → GUT → GVE → goal verify → GVD. Apply React, content/SEO and migration/release; add editor/schema only if an editor model is actually involved. - A WHMCS password-reset rate-limit repair combines diagnosis, tested implementation and security: GAS → diagnose → GPP → GPR → GTF → GTE → GUT → GVS → GVR. Verify allowed and denied attempts, account/IP policy, time windows and concurrency in the real installed version. - An HTML/ZIP-to-native-YAML import combines source fidelity and schema contracts: GDA + source inventory → GDS → GPP → GPR → GEX → import/round-trip tests → visual review. The current native-YAML and design-system plugins own their native component rules. - An automatic-router plugin update combines assessment, research, architecture and contract verification: GAS + GRS → GAA → GPP → GPR → GEX → GUT → GVR → GVD, followed by an authorised release and source readback. Test explicit command preservation and no-task handling. These examples do not confer publication, deployment, deletion, purchasing or communication authority. Use the current request and existing permissions. Do not import private histories or project secrets into the reusable plugin.

resources.title: Concrete modes, six families and useful teams
resources.summary: Apply this shared policy to Auto, explicit modes, every G/numeric control, recipe, quick task and continuation, with the workflow contract. The registry owns family/capability/legacy mappings; the runtime policy validates declared decisions. The host supplies source-grounded judgment, real dispatch and inspected results.
resources.body: Concrete modes, six families and useful teams Apply this shared policy to Auto, explicit modes, every G/numeric control, recipe, quick task and continuation, with the workflow contract. The registry owns family/capability/legacy mappings; the runtime policy validates declared decisions. The host supplies source-grounded judgment, real dispatch and inspected results. Select a concrete mode Exactly five public controls remain: auto , plan , build , review , loop . Auto selects one of the other four. Explicit advanced controls retain their requested phases, inputs, record semantics and write boundaries while resolving a concrete mode. Intent Mode Boundary --- --- --- Produce or revise a plan/specification Plan Planning and independent criticism; stop before product edits. Implement, fix, refactor, author tests or change project docs/artifacts Build Exact plan criticism, admission, implementation and independent acceptance. Research, diagnose, assess, audit, compare or check existing work Review Evidence and findings; no silent repair. Repeated independent review and repair until acceptance Loop Existing manager/executor/fresh-review cycle with five-minute monitoring. Investigation can be a read-only phase inside authorized Build. A finding does not authorize repair. Preserve audit-only, Plan-only, mockup-first and no-publish limits. Do not ask the user to select internal roles when the request and source establish the answer. Delegate useful work every time Every new logical task returns contributions from at least two distinct actual workers , excluding coordinator. Tiny, Plan, Review, research, verification and standalone commands have no single-worker exemption. A role path, agentCalls row, planned identity, status ping, failed dispatch, second profile on one actor or repeated summary without independent inspection does not count. A short source-grounded no-findings report can count; finding a defect is not a quota. The primary worker does useful work. A different worker supplies a specific independent check, challenge or corroboration. Writing tasks have independent current plan criticism before edits and acceptance after the stable integrated result. Plan/Review tasks obtain the second useful contribution before reporting completion without inventing implementation or a formal stage. Pass the original requirements/corrections, source baseline, selected record, bounded question, allowed paths/operations, selected capability instructions, output destination and decisive checks. Combine relevant domain lenses on actual workers; do not launch a worker for every keyword. Six canonical families Family Owns Scope boundary --- --- --- Investigator Research, assessment, diagnosis, behavior/invariants, contribution discovery Source/evidence work, no automatic repair. Architect and Planner Architecture, goal/code/test planning, dependencies and migration order Advice and planning. Builder Admitted implementation, Fast/Ponytail, TDD, cleanup, docs and delivery preparation Only assigned product/test/docs paths; no self-acceptance. UI Director Actual reference inventory, UI audit/specification, visual/interaction direction Design/advice, no competing implementation owner. Reviewer Independent plan criticism, source/outcome review, completeness and acceptance Read-only review, independent of substantive authors. Verification Engineer Actual tests, browser journeys, accessibility, security, performance and lifecycle checks Check outputs only; no fixes or weakened tests. Thirty-eight original role paths resolve through the registry to these families and required capabilities. The two reused core paths plus 36 compatibility entries remain meaningful and nonempty. They are not 38 active agents. The 21 domain lenses remain reusable knowledge. Resolve profile plus selected operation , not profile name alone. GCA/GEA writes are Builder work; review-only and check-only operations stay read-only. GJ test authoring, GTF RED-only, GTE GREEN/refactor, GVD docs-only and GPP planning retain their distinct boundaries. Select the route from inspected impact Before final routing, search the packaged task index provisionally from the literal request, inspect project/source evidence, and refine the query when ownership, stack or affected surfaces were initially unknown. Inspect the grouped shortlist; retrieval is candidate-only. 1. Resolve intent before speed. A quick inspection stays Plan or Review. 2. Investigate unknown cause, ownership or affected consumers before classifying/admitting repair. 3. Broad changes—multiple affected pages/features, changed shared contracts or architectural/ migration decisions—require Architect advice before the finalized plan and criticism. A one-line shared setting can require this; source file count is not impact. 4. Known bounded localized Build uses GB/Fast/Ponytail, with Builder's complete fast-build capability plus independent Reviewer. Fast reduces repeated reading/work, never contributors or gates. 5. Preserve explicit controls. G0 remains compact; applying Fast there does not allocate a second GB record. Explicit GB/G0/G1 cannot waive broad-impact advice or independent review. 6. Select UI and substantial-verification duties from inspected outcomes and exact acceptance. Do not guess these facts from keyword lists or report a descriptor as real dispatch. Which roles to assign Counts below exclude coordinator and describe contributors over the task, not simultaneous slots. Task Required team Expansion and preserved scope --- --- --- Small known localized Build Fast Builder + Reviewer Existing GB route; compact G0 stays compact. Plan only Architect/Planner + Reviewer Add Investigator for unresolved facts or UI Director for material design. No build. Research, assessment or diagnosis only Investigator + Reviewer Independently check a consequential claim, omission or counterexample. Standalone code/plan/spec review, including GVR/GPR Primary Reviewer + different Reviewer or Verifier Verifier checks an executable/rendered claim; otherwise second Reviewer checks a bounded claim. Preserve primary owner and selected operation. Check-only work Verification Engineer + Reviewer Independently check coverage and interpretation; no repairs. Unknown impact inside authorized repair Investigator first, then Builder + Reviewer Reuse compatible investigation/execution identity where useful; add Architect if broad impact emerges. Shared/multiple-page/feature or architectural Build Distinct Architect + Builder + Reviewer Advice before finalized plan/criticism. Track secondary authors too. Mechanical local UI label/token/component application Fast Builder with full UI expertise + UI-aware Reviewer Existing approved design, actual rendered check. New layout/palette/type/responsive/interaction design or reconstruction Distinct UI Director + Builder + Reviewer Actual design/state brief before accepted planning. UI Plan/Review adds no Builder. Shared UI/design-system Build Distinct Architect + UI Director + Builder + Reviewer Shared-consumer and visual contracts; use sequential waves. Substantial validation Add distinct Verification Engineer Multiple check families/environments, specialized measurement, lifecycle, substantial browser journeys, or explicit independent verification. Documentation/package work Builder with relevant capability + Reviewer Add Verifier for installation/runtime/lifecycle claims. Publication follows accepted output. Extra Builders need nonoverlapping ownership or isolated checkouts and one integrator. A second Reviewer must examine actual evidence, not merely endorse the first. Do not manufacture findings, repairs or wider scope to justify workers. Use the complete UI applicability and domain specialist instructions where relevant. Independence, contribution and synthesis Independence follows actual identity and all substantive authorship. Adopted architecture, UI specifications and plans cannot be independently criticized by their authors. Source, test, docs and integration authors cannot accept the resulting work. Include secondary contributors; changing a role label does not remove authorship. Ordinary criticism/raw factual collection is not automatically adopted solution authorship. A Reviewer that writes the solution becomes an author and needs another acceptor. One independent Reviewer may critique and later accept. Maintain the normal task's compact ledger, with each actual assignment/worker, concrete result, inspected evidence, limitations, current work/artifact/result revision, disposition and effect. Use incorporated , rejected with a reason, or unresolved ; unresolved in-scope work blocks completion. Empty limitations means no known material limit, not unexamined coverage. The coordinator reconciles evidence into one result. Disagreement is resolved through sources and the responsible owner/reviewer, not majority voting or several competing final answers. Acceptance covers the stable integrated output. A changed output revision reopens affected acceptance even when the plan remains valid. Author-run checks are useful evidence and remain separate from independent acceptance. No publication before required current contributions and acceptance; post-install readback naturally follows the installation it checks. Capacity and continuation Two useful contributors need not run concurrently. If one child slot is available, complete A, release it and dispatch different B. Report required contributors, useful returned contributors and active agents separately. Active count is coordinator plus workers actually running; completed/failed/queued workers add zero. Preserve real spawn/result receipts. Missing dispatch blocks dependent work, with permitted preparation and an honest checkpoint. Assigned children perform their bounded duty without recursively creating teams. Reuse valid completed evidence for unchanged continuation/status. Changed scope, source/result, adopted choices or stale contributions reopen affected work. Do not start new tasks for status questions. New executable records use contract-v2. Preserve archived v1 bytes; actively resumed records reconcile canonical aliases, actual IDs, all authors and missing contributions explicitly. Do not silently rehash old criticism or promote old single-worker work. Loop keeps manager-only accounting, sole repair executor and fresh Reviewer after each execution. A clean initial review requires independent Verifier corroboration and original Reviewer acknowledgement before acceptance, without an empty executor pass. Preserve the five-minute wait-first/timer-second protocol and supported user/browser control. Portable helpers check declarations, structure and revision bindings. They cannot authenticate workers, judge all prose quality, inspect undeclared source drift or intercept arbitrary host tools. Actual dispatch, meaningful work and substantive independent checking remain required host actions. Countercheck timing For Review, research and check-only completion, the second worker examines the primary inspection’s actual result after that result exists. A critique of the coordinator’s approach before inspection cannot replace the result countercheck. Plan may use criticism of the completed actual plan. This is a bounded duty inside the selected operation, not new write authority or a claim that an unselected numeric stage ran.

resources.title: Component diagnosis and repair
resources.summary: Read only the sections relevant to the current target after establishing its visual contract. Use these techniques to make an observed problem actionable. The current brief, approved reference, content source and receiving kit govern; an example here is not a new design preset. Keep findings and before/after evidence in the existing quality review.
resources.body: Component diagnosis and repair Read only the sections relevant to the current target after establishing its visual contract. Use these techniques to make an observed problem actionable. The current brief, approved reference, content source and receiving kit govern; an example here is not a new design preset. Keep findings and before/after evidence in the existing quality review. Contents 1. Choose the cause before the treatment 2. Terminals and static code illustrations 3. Badges, highlighted labels and icons 4. Hierarchy, density and typography 5. Vertical tabs and nested sections 6. Pricing and comparisons 7. Palette and artwork on the destination surface 8. Native-widget feasibility Choose the cause before the treatment Name the visual consequence before proposing a style change: for example, the label merges with its container edge, the illustration cannot be read at its displayed size, or the main action competes with several equally prominent elements. Identify the element and state. Trace the cause through the actual owner: missing/shared token, incorrect native preset, parent sizing, local override, font fallback, asset crop or the composition itself. Do not compensate for a wrong parent constraint with scattered child offsets. Resolve the effective cascade before diagnosing a missing inset or redundant enclosure. Inspect all rules that match the actual element, including specificity, :is() selectors, later style layers and active viewport/container conditions. A base declaration may already be reset by a more specific component rule. Use computed styles when available; in source-only review, cite the applicable override chain and label unresolved conditions instead of treating base CSS values as observed padding, borders or geometry. Choose a repair that addresses that cause and respects the task's mode. A local correction retains the approved composition; exploration may change it. A working simple layout can be deliberate. Explain what a proposed addition would communicate before adding it. Make each recommendation concrete: affected owner, changed relationship, expected visible effect, protected properties and a check capable of detecting failure. “More premium,” “better spacing” and “add interest” are diagnoses still waiting to be made. Terminals and static code illustrations Inspect. Identify the panel's job: a static illustration, source code, a command example, a live terminal or a language-switching demo. Inspect the supplied content contract first. Read the complete panel at the size it occupies beside the heading and body, then at narrow width. Diagnose. Separate an undersized outer panel from tiny internal type, oversized chrome, excessive internal empty space, a constrained parent column or a scaled-down image/SVG. Check whether the intended text is actual readable content or part of a bitmap/illustration. A large surrounding card does not make a small terminal inside it readable. Repair. Allocate enough width to the meaningful content, adjust the internal text scale within the approved type system, and balance header, body and inset proportions together. Let supplied short labels form a purposeful composition; avoid a large vacant shell. If a fixed-size visual is the cause, correct its layout or source asset rather than enlarging unrelated section padding. When rebalancing chrome and body spacing, inspect existing viewport and container overrides: a change that preserves desktop height can increase narrow-layout height. Preserve intentional scroll behaviour for genuine long code. Protect. Keep the illustration's actual labels, claims and role. A source that authorizes three static labels does not authorize fabricated shell commands, version numbers, logs, latency, deployment status or live telemetry. Do not add copy buttons or animation to make a static illustration appear more sophisticated. Preserve existing required controls when present. Verify. Inspect both the whole section and the panel at normal display size. Confirm each required label remains readable, chrome does not dominate it, and the mobile composition has no unintended clipping. For interactive panels, separately exercise each changed action/state. Record the native composition or actual custom-code constraint; terminal styling alone does not imply that executable or language-switching functionality is required. Badges, highlighted labels and icons Inspect. Examine the actual label box, glyph bounds, baseline and adjacent content. Check default, wrapped and relevant selected/hover states. Identify whether the label is a standalone badge, inline highlight, a control, or an item inside a larger card. Diagnose. Determine whether missing space belongs inside the colored label, between an icon and its text, between siblings, or around the parent. A roomy card cannot compensate for a badge whose letters touch its background edge. Check inherited line-height and display behaviour before prescribing a new margin or changing the type size. Repair. Apply insets to the label's actual owner using the appropriate shared badge/token or native part style. Coordinate horizontal and vertical breathing room with text size and shape. Use the component's gap/alignment controls for icon/text separation. Size icons by their visual weight as well as their box, and align them with the intended text line or group. Protect. Retain meaning, wording, semantic color and interaction. Do not turn a fact label into a button, replace the approved icon family, or change every badge because one local instance is wrong. When the shared owner is at fault, inspect its relevant consumers. Verify. Inspect real box edges and text at the required widths, including a longer/wrapped label where the content allows it. Confirm visible insets, intentional baseline alignment and no collision with adjoining copy. For controls, confirm focus visibility and the actual hit area. Hierarchy, density and typography Inspect. State the section's main message, supporting evidence and next action. Trace the reading order through the actual heading, paragraph, visual, facts and controls. Inspect the whole section before individual details; view the requested surrounding sections for context. Diagnose. Identify which relationship is weak: everything has equal emphasis; a minor label dominates; related items look disconnected; repeated containers conceal grouping; empty space separates a heading from its evidence; or important content is compressed. First confirm the actual loaded font and weight. Fallback fonts can change wraps, density and alignment, making downstream spacing changes a misleading repair. Repair. Establish clearer relative prominence with the existing type scale and spacing system. Group related content, distinguish meaningful groups and align shared reading edges. Adjust column proportions or text measure where allowed before shrinking all type to fit. Use surface contrast or selective emphasis where it clarifies a role; do not decorate every element equally. Recompose an underdeveloped section only to the extent authorized by its mode. Protect. Keep complete approved headings, copy and content order unless their change is authorized. Do not shorten copy, add invented statistics, split facts into extra cards or insert illustrations just to fill space. Preserve deliberate quietness and compact density when they suit the approved design and task. Avoid imposing a universal section height. Verify. Compare the before/after section at matching conditions. Explain how the primary message is easier to find or the content relationships are clearer. Check resulting wraps, reading length, action visibility and responsive order. An absence of overflow is only one check; it does not establish a well-composed result. Vertical tabs and nested sections Inspect. Read the approved grouping and inspect every requested tab panel, not only the initial panel. Distinguish the selector, panel shell, heading/card structure and nested content. Identify content explicitly required outside the tabs and preserve that placement. Diagnose. Trace uneven edges or cramped panels to selector width, nested padding, reused card presets, unnecessary wrapper layers or different content owners. Check whether a short panel is being stretched to imitate a long one and whether duplicated headings add false hierarchy. Repair. Reuse the prescribed selector and panel composition. Make shared inner edges, heading treatments and content insets consistent through their canonical owners. Let legitimate content differences remain visible; change sizing only where the reference or current brief requires it. Use the actual native nesting contract rather than flattening panels into raw HTML. Protect. Keep tab count, labels, order, default selection and source-specific panel content. Preserve working keyboard/focus behaviour and the approved narrow-screen adaptation. A visual repair does not authorize new categories, a different navigation pattern or moving external sections. Verify. Open each required panel and compare its heading, body, controls and lower edge. Exercise changed navigation at relevant widths. For native exports, check the documented pairing of item entries and panel hosts, preview the payload, and report editor round-trip access separately. Pricing and comparisons Inspect. Read across adjacent plans/columns and down equivalent specification rows. Check plan name, price, period, renewal/discount explanation, action and details as one hierarchy. Inspect long labels, highlighted plans, outer edges and narrow-screen table behaviour. Diagnose. Distinguish row misalignment from text wrapping, inconsistent content groups, different card padding, independent heights, hidden details or a misplaced action. Check whether emphasis helps the intended comparison or makes every column equally loud. Repair. Reuse the existing pricing/table owner and align equivalent information at that owner. Coordinate label space, content spacing and action placement without changing facts. Apply the requested shared borders, gaps and corner treatment consistently; those choices are project contracts, not universal pricing rules. Preserve deliberate horizontal scrolling. Protect. Keep plan identities, prices, units, billing periods, qualifiers, entitlements, button destinations and default expansion. Do not invent a “recommended” or “best value” claim. Changing a shared presentation preset must not overwrite per-plan data or row-specific styles. Verify. Compare all affected columns and shared consumers, including the first/last edges. Confirm the price and its qualifier remain associated, equivalent rows scan coherently and controls remain usable. Compare the actual exported state with the selected preview. Palette and artwork on the destination surface Inspect. Place the real artwork on its actual page/hero background. Review the composition with nearby type, borders, actions and interaction states. Inspect transparent edges and dark/light variants at their intended display size; an isolated image preview cannot establish harmony. Diagnose. Separate a palette-role conflict from excessive saturation, competing accents, insufficient foreground separation, an incorrect asset variant or a visible compositing rectangle. Check whether the material itself or its background is causing the clash before recoloring either. Repair. Assign approved colors clear roles and use the subset that serves this composition. Tune their relative prominence within the authorized scope. Preserve enough contrast to keep text and meaningful visual boundaries legible. Correct the asset/crop/compositing owner when that is the cause; a global surface change may merely move the mismatch elsewhere. Protect. Retain approved brand roles, material/geometry, transparency and semantic state colors. A request for restraint does not mean removing all color. A different project does not inherit this project's palette. Recoloring

resources.title: UI correction playbook
resources.summary: Apply the rules relevant to the current brief. Each rule includes an acceptance check. The machine-readable rules use the same identifiers. Use project-specific values only when the current brief or approved design system supplies them.
resources.body: UI correction playbook Apply the rules relevant to the current brief. Each rule includes an acceptance check. The machine-readable rules use the same identifiers. Use project-specific values only when the current brief or approved design system supplies them. UI-001 — Define the current visual contract Applies to: All visual requests. Classify the task as exact reconstruction, bounded adaptation, exploration or local correction. Record actual target inventory, presentation source, content source, allowed changes and protected properties. Reconcile later feedback only within its subject and scope; do not promote historic requests into current commands. Check: Each target has a current brief and protected properties. Styling-only work preserves supplied copy and behaviour. A rejected concept is replaced only when replacement is requested. UI-002 — Trace the canonical component owner and reuse it Applies to: Existing interfaces and approved donor templates. Inspect the existing UI and trace the shared component, design token, preset and data owner before editing. Reuse approved navigation, table, settings and editor primitives. Do not invent tabs, notices, CTAs or new duplicate sections when the task is a local repair. Check: Shared consumers receive consistent changes. Existing navigation, controls, data ownership and complete setting inventories remain functional. Protected component structures survive scoped content patches. UI-003 — Separate target content from template presentation Applies to: Template adaptation, SEO pages and grouped designs. Use the approved template for layout and the correct page source for copy and facts. Preserve locked headings and wording; adapt only authorized subject-specific values. Sharing a design does not share instance copy. Detect renamed donor clones and stale donor facts. Check: Every supplied heading and required content block maps to output. Each target is checked against its own source. No invented product claims, timings or replacement copy are introduced by visual polish. UI-004 — Assess deliberate visual quality, not merely validity Applies to: Layout, banner and gallery creation or review. Critique composition, hierarchy, proportion, visual density, content purpose and meaningful detail in every target. Distinguish broken usability from basic but underdeveloped design. When a new concept is requested, change its underlying idea and composition instead of recolouring rejected work. Simplification must retain enough meaning and interest. Check: Every target has a specific quality finding or a reasoned acceptable result. Improvement proposals name affected components and actionable changes. Native editor feasibility is recorded for proposed layout changes where relevant. UI-005 — Use a coherent palette in its actual surface context Applies to: Visual colour and material choices. Use the current design system and a deliberate coordinated subset of colours. Inspect artwork against its real hero or page background. Preserve purposeful colour when feedback rejects playfulness; avoid an all-green or colourless overcorrection. Show requested identifying card colours in the default visible state. Check: Background, artwork, accents, text and interactions are inspected together. Palettes preserve brand role and useful hierarchy. Material recolours preserve approved geometry and camera. UI-006 — Verify typography and font loading Applies to: Any visual typography change or inherited font contract. Use supplied font assets and canonical typography tokens across all consumers. Inspect the computed font, fallback loading, weight, size, line height, wrapping and contrast in the rendered output. Treat explicit size caps as scoped requirements. Check: Actual rendered font matches the supplied asset. Headings, body, labels, buttons and terminal text form an intentional readable scale. No clipped or avoidably wrapped action labels remain at supported widths. UI-007 — Inspect spacing, alignment and component proportions Applies to: All visual components. Measure rendered section and card padding, row baselines, grids, icon gaps, badge insets, button spacing and terminal proportions against the actual template or current design system. Fix the whole affected family. Inherit native presets instead of adding arbitrary local overrides. Check: Sibling columns and rows align intentionally. Badges and highlighted text have visible suitable insets. Cards, headings and controls are symmetrical where the design requires it. Responsive changes preserve readable proportions without clipping. UI-008 — Preserve and exercise real UI behaviour Applies to: Interactive applications and editor tools. Review the actual user journey and expected state ownership. Controls must perform their stated action; focus must not retarget unrelated sessions or files. Test meaningful changed behaviour, including empty and populated states, rather than relying on a screenshot. Check: Filters, density controls, folders, panels, modal controls and actions operate correctly. Disabled background work actually stops when that is the requirement. Focus and navigation do not unexpectedly mutate unrelated views or state. UI-009 — Reconcile every requested target and state Applies to: All batch, family, gallery and multi-state requests. Build the actual inventory from supplied files and requested targets. Treat user examples as diagnostic examples, not a reduced scope. Review every included layout and relevant hidden panel, palette, default state, viewport and exported variant. Deduplicate by content and intended identity; retain distinct requested variants. Check: A per-ID matrix reconciles requested, inspected, repaired, blocked and delivered items. Each tab and FAQ panel is inspected where requested. Contact sheets support full-size review and do not replace it. The target count comes from evidence; an approximate historic number is not hardcoded. UI-010 — Perform rendered visual critique and report its limits Applies to: Visual implementation and visual audit. Open the actual final output in an available authorized rendering environment. Inspect desktop and mobile plus relevant interactions and full animation cycles. Record named defects, repair authorized defects, and rerun affected checks. Separate schema, source, screenshot, temporal and destination-import evidence. Check: Evidence records target ID, output revision, viewport/state and observation. A successful build or validator is never reported as proof of visual quality. Blocked rendering is explicitly marked unverified; no fabricated screenshots or checks. Review-only requests remain review-only. UI-011 — Maintain native editor editability Applies to: Tasks whose receiving format is native YAML or another editor schema. Read the authoritative kit and approved native template. Map content to supported widgets, nesting and presets. Honor native-only requirements and only specifically authorized custom-code exceptions. Proposed improvements must describe a real supported widget composition. Check: All generated widget types and properties pass the supplied validator. The complete content inventory is represented. Forbidden custom-code widgets are absent. A source HTML lookalike cannot substitute for a native editable payload. UI-012 — Preview the actual import payload and verify round trips Applies to: Native editor deliverables. Generate or verify HTML from the final native payload and provide it before user import when requested. Compare its source, hierarchy, content and rendered state with the supplied references. When access exists, verify import, editing, saving and reopening; otherwise state which parts remain untested. Check: Each target has an independently openable matching preview. Preview and native export identify the same revision. Large previews are split only when the task or practical limits require it. Syntax, schema, render and receiving-editor checks are separately reported. UI-013 — Use the correct asset and preserve reference identity Applies to: Image, icon, animation and archived visual retrieval. Identify the exact source artifact, variant and latest applicable revision before work. Inspect references; keep approved silhouette, geometry, pose, angle, composition and content outside the requested change. Find real existing-site icons where required. Do not substitute a still, renamed image or unrelated gallery for a requested animation. Check: Retrieved assets contain the requested concepts and variants. CAD remains genuine drawing rather than a desaturated photograph. Recolour-only output preserves other protected properties. Mismatches are described instead of asserting unsupported perfect fidelity. UI-014 — Inspect production image quality and compositing Applies to: Raster, CAD and render assets. Inspect full-size outputs on their actual destination surface. Check edges, transparency, clipped reflections, geometry, materials, illumination and transitions. Register CAD and realistic layers using fixed landmarks. Preserve source originals and separately requested variants. Check: No visible rectangle, pasted cutout or clipped reflection breaks the intended compositing. Material and geometry match the authorized reference. Exported resolution and real detail are inspected, not inferred from file dimensions. UI-015 — Preserve persona traits and natural anatomy Applies to: Requested persona or people imagery only. Follow supplied persona prompts and reference traits while creating original brand-appropriate compositions. Inspect hands, pose, faces, texture and nearby callouts at display size and high zoom. Apply no-people or no-pointing constraints only to their named asset set. Check: Every person matches the applicable persona reference. Hands, joints, body balance and facial rendering appear natural. Callouts and imagery relate to the target page. People-only and text/no-text variants remain complete. UI-016 — Make motion communicate a meaningful sequence Applies to: Animated visual widgets and transitions. Model the intended request, response, action or transformation before animating. Preserve approved geometry and paths; avoid arbitrary moving blocks. Verify startup, stages, readable holds, pacing, loop/stop behaviour, controls and a complete cycle. Timing belongs to its asset and latest scoped instruction. Check: API/MCP or other semantic motion communicates the actual intended relationship. Markers stay on paths and layers remain registered. The requested playable format is delivered. Source sequence revisions do not become global duration or looping defaults. UI-017 — Keep shared design, instance copy and persisted state distinct Applies to: Configurable studios and reusable design families. Trace shared design choices separately from per-page content and per-item selections. Group design changes must preserve page-specific copy. Persist choices in the intended store, restore them on reopen and reflect them in previews and exports. Restore requested presets and individual editing. Check: Group and individual changes affect only the expected owners. Save/reload recovers the selected values. Each copy preset populates all its intended fields. A download-to-desktop is not called server persistence. UI-018 — Verify export parity, isolation and dependency closure Applies to: HTML/CSS/JS widgets, native wrappers and asset packages. Export exactly the selected content, palette and enabled controls in the required format. Remove disabled presentation controls and unused palette definitions from source when required. Scope widget markup, CSS and runtime to a unique root. Reconcile standalone and bulk exports with previews and the requested inventory. Check: Two widgets mounted together do not interfere. Individual and bulk downloads reproduce selected appearance and behaviour. Required native wrappers use their inherited presets. Requested source stripping is verified across HTML, CSS and JavaScript. UI-019

resources.title: Visual quality review and complete target coverage
resources.summary: Establish the expected set
resources.body: Visual quality review and complete target coverage Establish the expected set Read the real source inventory and current request. Enumerate each requested page/layout/component, asset variant and required state. Preserve stable IDs. Treat a stated approximate count as a clue; resolve the actual count from the files. Examples such as one poor terminal or badge are diagnostic seeds for an all-layout review, not permission to inspect only those examples. Use the existing task record and acceptance evidence. Record the expected set before repair, so a failed target cannot disappear from the denominator. Keep a compact correction table for a single local edit; do not impose a batch manifest on a trivial repair. Inspect the actual output Open every requested target in the relevant browser, native application, editor renderer or image viewer. Inspect full-size readable content, relevant below-fold regions and hidden panels. A contact sheet is a navigation aid. Inspect affected desktop, intermediate and small viewport behaviour according to the current target contract, including intentional internal table scrolling. Load actual fonts and assets. Observe full meaningful animation cycles and changed transitions where motion is in scope. Keep source and output comparable: revision, viewport, zoom, data, theme, font, selected tab and timing. Measure geometry from the runtime where available; label screenshot estimates as estimates. Confirm that the page being reviewed is the actual final output rather than a stale preview. Use available authorized browser/rendering capabilities and the kit's real tools; do not invent unavailable commands. Review working layouts as critically as broken ones Dimension Concrete inspection --- --- Purpose and hierarchy Is the main idea and next action clear? Do heading, copy and visual reinforce it? Composition and density Are relationships deliberate, proportions balanced and useful detail sufficient? Is empty space serving the composition? Spacing and alignment Check real outer/inner padding, highlighted-text insets, card gaps, baselines, icons, button groups and sibling edges. Typography Confirm loaded family, weights, scale, line-height, wrapping, line length and readable labels/terminal output. Palette and surfaces Inspect foreground, background, artwork, borders and hover/focus/selected states together. Use a coherent subset of approved colours. Components A terminal needs believable proportions and readable task-appropriate content; a badge needs padding; a comparison needs scannable aligned information. Assets and identity Check correct source/variant, crop, edges, transparency, geometry, material, persona traits and destination-surface harmony. Behaviour and access Exercise changed actions, keyboard/focus, pending/error/empty states, overflow and persistence. Remove duplicate focus rings without removing focus visibility. Native feasibility Map each proposal to actual supported widget types, fields, nested structure and presets in the supplied kit. Export and delivery Verify selected copy/palette/settings survive the actual native/standalone export and intended opening context. A clean build, valid YAML or absence of clipping does not establish deliberate design quality. Identify underdeveloped but working layouts, repetitive default compositions, weak hierarchy, oversized empty areas, cramped meaningful content and decorative detail with no purpose. Each recommendation must explain a concrete visual change and its effect. Respect approved simplicity and reconstruction targets; quality improvement does not authorize new copy, extra features or a different brand. Use component diagnosis and repair for the affected component family. Name the actual owner and cause before prescribing a treatment; measure the visible relationship that should change. Preserve deliberately simple work and source-only illustrations. Record findings in the existing evidence artifacts For each target retain these fields in its review table or linked observation: Target ID Output/source revision Viewport/state Observed issue Functional severity Improvement potential Concrete change Protected properties Native mapping/feasibility Evidence Recheck state Functional severity can be blocking, major, minor or none. Improvement potential is a separate judgment of how much a composition can benefit: high, medium, low or already deliberate. Explain both from observations. Avoid arbitrary self-awarded quality scores. A target with no blocking defects still needs a reasoned quality assessment. Native feasibility is not applicable to non-editor work; if the kit is missing, record the mapping as unresolved instead of inventing widget support. When multiple observations share a cause, link a family finding while keeping every target's inspection and result visible. Report all requested issues; prioritization may order the report, not omit less urgent targets. Clearly distinguish a user's reported defect from a defect independently observed now. Historical labels such as B13/M04 do not establish exact geometry without their source visuals. Repair and verify For authorized changes, fix the canonical owner with the smallest complete scoped change. Recheck every affected target and protected neighbour required by the contract, including shared consumers. Verify that the original complaint is observably resolved and that changes did not remove approved details. For audit-only work, deliver the complete actionable findings and native feasibility without editing. State requested, inspected, repaired, rechecked, unresolved and delivered counts separately. Every required target/state needs current evidence; unobserved or inaccessible results remain blocked or not-run. A sampled inspection must never become an exhaustive visual claim. Do not call the result perfect, user-approved or fully verified when any requested outcome remains unobserved.

resources.title: Automatic UI expertise and team selection
resources.summary: Decide from the requested outcome
resources.body: Automatic UI expertise and team selection Decide from the requested outcome Assess the complete current task, adopted corrections, source and selected record. Apply specialist:ui-design whenever the outcome creates, changes, assesses or repairs presentation, interaction design, visual quality or visual assets. Apply it alongside relevant stack/format knowledge, including follow-ups such as “the spacing is still wrong.” An ordinary attached skill and explicit Auto use the same rule. Outcome Relevant knowledge --- --- Layouts, websites, sections, cards, tables, dashboards and navigation UI design plus the actual frontend/platform owner. Colors, palettes, typography, spacing, alignment, proportions and icons UI design; design-system for shared owners; reference-fidelity for approved baselines. Visual audit, critique or improvement proposal UI knowledge within the selected read-only/Plan scope. Native YAML, HTML/template conversion or editor presentation UI plus native-yaml/editor-schema and the receiving kit. Hero/CTA artwork, renders, image variants or reference-image corrections UI plus image-art-direction/reference-fidelity and actual image tools. Animation, demos, tabs/carousels and transitions UI plus motion-interaction; inspect complete temporal behavior. Filters, controls, focus, state, accessibility or feedback UI plus the actual interaction/state owner. Pure backend/data/infrastructure work without a visible outcome is not UI work. Quoted old requests, a color word in data or a frontend directory alone prove no applicability. Policy work about UI does not itself authorize a website redesign. Image-only work uses actual image inspection; native desktop work uses its real runtime rather than an invented browser. Classify the design contribution Every v2 task declares actual UI facts: kind Meaning Required staffing --- --- --- none No requested visual/interaction outcome; applicable is false. The task's nonvisual team; no invented UI work. mechanical Apply an existing approved local label, token or component without new design decisions. UI-capable Fast Builder and independent UI-aware Reviewer for Build. design Decide layout, palette, type, responsiveness, interaction or reference reconstruction. Distinct UI Director before accepted planning; Builder and Reviewer for Build. shared Change shared UI/design-system decisions or consumer contracts. Architect and UI Director plus Builder/Reviewer for Build, using waves if needed. The kind is an inspected fact, not a keyword classifier or speed waiver. New design cannot be labeled mechanical to omit the UI Director. Shared UI cannot be classified local just because one file changes. UI-only Plan/Review obtains useful design and independent criticism/corroboration without adding a Builder or product writes. Carry complete expertise into actual work Read the full UI expertise, UI Director and relevant capability instructions. Pass complete applicable knowledge to actual design, implementation and independent review workers. Declare ui-design on their assignments and record actual assignment-to-worker bindings and contributions. A specialist catalogue row, profile name or summary alone proves no dispatch. A separate UI Director is required for design/shared work, with the real source/reference/state brief before the affected plan and criticism. Mechanical work may combine UI expertise with Builder; rendered acceptance remains independent. Relevant operations remain authoritative: - Audit/review/research: inspect and report, no repairs. - Plan/specification: implementable direction and measurable acceptance, no build. - Mockup-first: deliver the agreed mockup and preserve its implementation boundary. - Authorized Build: implement the admitted scope and independently check its visual result. - Help/no-task/status: preserve current selection; a policy pointer starts no invented task. Inspect approved references, existing tokens/components, requested pages, viewports and states. Verify actual rendering and relevant interactions. Record what remains unverified; markup, schema and build success cannot establish visual parity. Domain kits/editor/image tools keep their real ownership. Respect explicit current user exclusions through truthful scope/policy reconciliation rather than falsely declaring non-UI applicability or pretending a gate passed. Selection, validation and continuation Select specialist:ui-design when applicable. Existing explicit visual operations require it; a false/omitted applicability field cannot waive their knowledge requirement. Legacy evaluated rows may remain source evidence, but active v2 records need the full current declaration. Record substantive UI authors in authorIds ; they cannot independently criticize their adopted specification or accept the resulting design by changing profiles. The router describes required duties from supplied uiContext and verification facts. It does not render, dispatch or inspect the request itself. Source/capability changes affect catalogue and policy fingerprints. Reconcile affected pending work while preserving current verified outcomes. Use task routing, contract records and real rendered evidence to complete the task.

resources.title: Public versioning policy
resources.summary: Product and public release identity
resources.body: Public versioning policy Product and public release identity The product name is AI Development Workflow . Human-facing headings, plugin display names and agent metadata use that plain name without a version suffix. The public release tag is 2.0 . It is the concise public release presentation, not a replacement for the source and package machine version. Machine package identity: 2.0.0 The internal source/package SemVer is 2.0.0 . Keep VERSION , both plugin manifest version fields, the 2.0.0 changelog key and package-content metadata aligned. The canonical builder derives archive filenames from VERSION , so its current archive names remain ai-development-workflow-v2.0.0-local-skill.zip and ai-development-workflow-v2.0.0-plugin.zip ; do not hardcode the public 2.0 presentation into machine package names. For this corrective Release, external staging renames those exact verified bytes to ai-development-workflow-2.0-local-skill.zip and ai-development-workflow-2.0-plugin.zip before generating SHA256SUMS.txt from the final basenames. Display identity and machine identity are separate contracts. A plain product heading must not be rejected because it omits SemVer, and a correct display name must never excuse a mismatched manifest or package version. Corrective replacement of the v2.0.0 release The earlier v2.0.0 Git tag and same-named GitHub release were created with incorrect public presentation. The owner authorized replacing that release with tag 2.0 , removing the old GitHub Release and deleting only its v2.0.0 tag ref after the replacement is public and verified. The corrective commit remains a normal descendant: do not rewrite, force-push or retrospectively relabel commit history. The replacement archives retain internal package version 2.0.0 . Previously downloaded v2.0.0 assets cannot be recalled and may differ from the corrective replacement bytes; release notes and checksums must state the replacement honestly. Public commit 9df3b6b also carried an untagged mistaken/preparatory higher patch source label before the formal release. It is a historical source snapshot, not the active product identity or an instruction to recreate a higher release. Consumers that copied that source may observe the normalized machine version as a numerical downgrade; source normalization does not automatically downgrade an installed plugin. Next machine patch After this explicitly authorized corrective replacement, the next machine package release is 2.0.1 , followed by 2.0.2 and later patches. Do not reuse 2.0.0 again, and do not change the 2.0 major/minor line unless the owner explicitly requests it. Before preparing a release, compare the current source, tags and published releases. A proposed title is publication metadata, not the active source version, and a prepared candidate is not a published release. Schema versions, protocol revisions and independently versioned integration packages are separate identifiers. Preserve them unless their own contract is deliberately changed; never apply a global version substitution. Validate generated archives and their machine version fields before an authorized publication.

resources.body: Mandatory workflow contract Apply this contract to every invocation : automatic selection, explicit G/numeric commands, public modes, named advanced handlers, quick tasks, recipes, internal operations, corrections and continuation. It governs all roles and takes precedence over older plugin wording that permits omitted planning, criticism, real delegation or announcements. Apply the authoritative task routing policy: every task resolves Plan, Build, Review or Loop and requires useful contributions from at least two distinct actual workers, excluding coordinator. Auto is the selector. A selected command retains its requested outcome and write scope; it cannot waive these prerequisites. Do not ask the user to repeat this contract. Contents - Open with the actual contract - Plan and criticize before work - Admit product changes - Report phases and real agents - Reuse and invalidate evidence - Recover truthfully - Enforcement boundary Open with the actual contract Before substantive task work, send the user a concise visible brief containing: 1. Scope: requested outcome, intended deliverable and important boundaries/protected behavior. 2. Selection: concrete mode, chosen workflow/recipe or composed chain, inspected impact and the reason the required roles fit. Auto must report the concrete mode it selected. 3. Phases: numbered, ordered phases with actual statuses and the current phase. 4. Owners: actual or planned worker assignment for each task phase; distinguish any coordinator self-check of a read-only approach from required independent criticism. 5. Agents: required/returned contributor counts and numeric count of the coordinator plus actually running workers. List planned workers separately. Applied specialist profiles are expertise and add zero agents. 6. Admission: implementation is pending until the current plan, completed criticism and declared briefing satisfy their admission checks. Never announce a gate passed before it did. Use progress announcements for messages and transitions. If the workspace or suitable workflow is unknown, first announce provisional read-only reconnaissance, its narrow approach and limitations, and actual agent count. Inspect only what is needed to identify the owners and ground the scope/plan. Then confirm the selected chain before dependent work. This exception permits no product change and no silent full assessment. Plan and criticize before work Every task has captured scope, a proportional plan and actual criticism of that plan. The depth follows the job; the prerequisites do not disappear because a task looks easy. Requested work Required preparation Preserved boundary --- --- --- Build, fix, test authoring, cleanup or project documentation Concrete changes, owners, dependency order, protected behavior and decisive checks; completed criticism of that exact plan before writes Only authorized product/test/docs changes G0 quick correction Compact scope, steps/checks, actual execution worker, independent criticism/result review and briefing in its existing quick record No automatic six-file promotion or second GB record; no solo exemption Research, assessment, review, verification or planning only Brief operation plan and criticism of its assumptions, source access, coverage and limits; may be recorded in the existing brief/evidence No application implementation or fabricated build history Continuation with exact current evidence Reconcile source and completed work, reuse the valid plan/criticism, publish the current phase/roster No needless allocation or replay of completed phases Task-record and evidence writes needed to capture, plan, criticize and record outcomes are allowed within their assigned scope before product admission. They are not project-documentation implementation. Advanced planning-only operations such as numeric 1/01, GPL or GCP may stop with the implementation critique pending; they still critically check their planning approach and report that product execution is not admitted. The primary Plan mode includes completed criticism of the resulting plan before it reports completion. No planning-only mode authorizes product edits. Criticism must examine the actual source and exact proposed changes: scope authority, feasibility, dependency order, verification, and protected behavior. Record concrete findings and their dispositions, or a grounded explanation of why no material finding remains. Resolve blocking findings and review the corrected plan. A risk list, an unfinished self-check, a nonempty critique file or a ready flag alone is insufficient. Every new logical task has at least two useful actual worker contributions, including Plan, read-only and standalone operations. Every product/test/docs writer, including G0/G1/GB, is a real execution specialist and needs a distinct real critic of the current plan and independent acceptance of the result. A role name or coordinator self-critique cannot satisfy these duties. Read-only tasks obtain a primary contribution and a distinct consequential corroboration within the selected operation. Coordinator inspection-approach self-checks do not replace either worker. Architect advice for broad/shared impact must finish before final plan completion and criticism. Preserve Loop's stronger fresh-reviewer requirements: its reviewer confirms the repair plan and owns substantive acceptance; its manager only coordinates and reconciles accounting. Admit product changes Before the first product source, test or project-documentation write, and before resumed writes after interruption, require all of the following: - Original request/corrections and scope are captured in the selected record. - Concrete plan and verification coverage match the authorized outcome and current source. - A concrete mode, source-grounded routing decision and required delegation assignments are declared; started worker phases have actual non-coordinator owners and applied profiles. - Required Architect advice is complete before the affected final plan and criticism; unknown impact cannot masquerade as a localized fast build. - Completed, revision-bound criticism has no unresolved blocker and covers the selected mutation operations, scopes and dependency order. - Scope, workflow, phases/owners and actual agent count have been visibly communicated. - The current declared briefing and review bindings pass the applicable admission helper. - The executor has actually reconciled relevant source/diff, permissions and other writers. - Every adopted architecture/design/plan author participates in the independence check; final acceptance excludes every source/test/docs/integration author and binds the final stable result. The coordinator may integrate, package and perform already-authorized publication after specialist execution and independent acceptance. This does not authorize taking over the assigned implementation silently. Required workers may run sequentially; unavailable dispatch blocks dependent task work. Children execute their existing bounded assignment without recursively creating another mandatory worker chain. For a development record, use record gates and scripts/resolve plan record.py --execution with the exact project/record. Criticism is mandatory even without --require-critique ; that compatibility flag cannot relax admission. For interrupted execution use the documented explicit --resume flow. For G0, use its shared compact contract and commands/quick-task/scripts/audit task record.py <record --execution . A plain record resolve, traceability audit, router descriptor or planned finalization grants no execution admission. Where the required helper cannot run, keep product execution blocked and complete permitted preparation; do not invent a pass or an alternative bypass. Numeric 013 , 13 , 3 , direct executors, GVD documentation and GCL cleanup retain their requested operations. Announce and fulfill missing capture/plan/criticism prerequisites before writes, or reuse their exact valid coverage. Never silently interpret a missing digit as a waiver. Do not turn a read-only or plan-only request into a build. All selected product-writing operations require the current reviewed plan; a missing catalogue Boolean cannot disable the gate. Repair authorization identifies permitted findings and does not replace criticism of the concrete repair. Continuing writes remain bound to the same authorized work definition; material unrelated drift requires renewed planning and criticism. Report phases and real agents Statuses mean pending , in progress , complete , or blocked based on evidence. Do not mark a partial critique complete, or combine “implement and verify” into a completed phase while verification is missing. Before a transition, state the completed phase and its actual result, the next phase and owner, and the current numeric agent count. Before delegation, announce the proposed assignment; only after a successful spawn report it as launched using the real returned identity. Keep coordinator/current agent, running workers, completed/failed workers, planned workers, and applied profiles distinct. Queued stages, reserved identities and agentCalls metadata are not running agents. If dispatch fails, report the real count and fallback. Required independence cannot be simulated by renaming the current agent. Routine tools within an unchanged phase need no repeated opening brief. Record the actual public briefing after emitting it, including its text/context and current bindings. Producing text in a helper or writing a local file is not publishing it to the user. Never manufacture an announcement receipt. Follow the same rule for completion statements. Before completion, every required assignment has a useful current contribution with result, inspected evidence, limitations, revision, disposition and effect on synthesis. At least two different workers qualify. Unresolved in-scope obligations remain open. Before publication, required preceding contributions and independent acceptance of the exact prepared result must exist; post-install checks still follow installation. Reuse and invalidate evidence Preserve one task record, original messages, stable requirement IDs and prior evidence. New execution uses contract-v2. Archived v1 records remain byte-identical; active reconciliation preserves old receipts and actual identities and obtains missing current evidence instead of silently rehashing criticism. Changed requirements, plan definitions, relevant source assumptions, or selected mutation operations/scopes/order need reconciliation and renewed criticism of affected work. resources.body: Portable workflow contract records Apply the workflow contract and team routing. These are portable declarations, not authenticated worker/chat receipts or proof of review quality. The host must dispatch real workers, inspect source/evidence and emit actual briefings. Contents - Location and explicit migration - Selection and assignments - Actual workers and authors - Useful contributions and current results - Criticism and bindings - Author, announce and admit - Completion validation - Compact G0 Location and explicit migration Development records retain schema: project-development-plan/v1 , contractVersion: 2 , their six files, source provenance and stable R/P/T mappings. The executable workflowContract object now uses ai-development-workflow/contract-v2 . G0 retains its existing request.md and checklist.md , with one workflow-contract.json in the same directory. A compact task is not promoted to six files merely to satisfy staffing. Archived v1 records and XR evidence retain their original bytes/hashes. Inspect them as history. Active execution or completion requires explicit current reconciliation. This read-only helper prints a proposal without editing the record, inventing contributions or admitting execution: Add --kind quick for G0. The result contains sourceContractHash , proposedContract , requiredActions and executionAdmitted: false . It retains the original parsed contract under legacyEvidence.contract and actual roster identities/evidence, with new declarations pending. Preserve the old record snapshot before adopting any proposal. Reconcile the actual selected mode, aliases, operations, scope, all authors and valid outputs; obtain missing contributions and current criticism. Never promote an old single-worker result or silently rehash its old review. A pending template/proposal is preparation, not permission to work alone or edit product files. Selection and assignments Field Required declaration --- --- schema ai-development-workflow/contract-v2 . selection.workflow , reason Actual workflow/command/recipe/composition and source-grounded reason. selection.selectionSchema , discovery New selections use ai-development-workflow/selection-v2 and a current ai-development-workflow/discovery-v1 receipt. Legacy selections remain readable but require discovery reconciliation before new execution. selection.mode Concrete plan , build , review or loop . Auto/XR are selector/alias provenance, not unresolved execution modes. selection.originMode Optional selector provenance, e.g. Auto. selection.routing Exact inspected impact fields below. selection.uiContext Boolean applicable , kind: none mechanical design shared , and concrete reason . False applies only to none. selection.verificationContext Boolean required , unique triggers and concrete reason ; required is true exactly when triggers are nonempty. selection.reviewPolicy Independent criticism for writing/Plan and selected independent-review work. Any permitted self-check of a read-only approach does not replace two useful workers or independent corroboration. selection.phases Ordered id , title , kind , operation , writeScope , dependsOn , owner . Dependencies refer only to preceding phases. selection.delegation policy: required , concrete reason , nonempty source evidence and required assignments. Routing has exactly impact , affectedPages , affectedFeatures , changedSharedContract , architectureOrMigration , reason , evidence . Impact is unknown , small-localized , standard or cross-cutting . Page/feature lists identify changed outcomes/consumers rather than all inspected files. Known-impact flags are booleans; genuinely unknown flags can be null. Unknown impact cannot admit repair or pretend to qualify for Fast. Broad Build obtains actual Architect advice before final planning/criticism and distinct Architect/Builder/Reviewer identities. Verification triggers are multiple-families , multiple-environments , specialized-measurement , lifecycle , substantial-browser-journeys , independent-deliverable . Use real acceptance needs, not keyword matches. A trigger requires a distinct Verification Engineer's contribution. UI classification follows UI routing; every applicable task uses full UI expertise. Each assignment has exactly these fields: IDs are unique; capabilities are nonempty unique registry IDs compatible with the resolved family. Resolve a supported legacy profile by selected operation and explicit capability mapping. Family is derived, not independently duplicated. The operation/write scope remains authoritative. A capability is knowledge, not authority for extra stages, writes, installation or publication. independentFrom names distinct other selected phases. Include every affected substantive architecture/design/plan/source/integration phase. A separate bounded corroboration phase inside a standalone operation does not claim an unrequested numeric stage ran. The primary Reviewer of GVR/GPR stays Reviewer; the second actual Reviewer/Verifier examines a consequential claim. For artifacts/workflow-selection.json , use the same current mode , routing , uiContext , verificationContext , delegation , reviewPolicy and phases , alongside the catalogue's existing selection fields/fingerprint. Do not maintain a weaker duplicate staffing definition. The router's optional --decision accepts exactly mode , routing , uiContext , verificationContext . It supplies diagnostic routing/duties, not actual worker evidence or execution admission. The discovery receipt contains the literal initial query, optional source-refined query, current index fingerprint, compact matched shortlist, selected IDs with reasons/instruction paths/worker questions/acceptance criteria, and one selected-or-not-applicable disposition for every specialist recommended by a selected recipe. It does not require full-catalogue evaluation. Paths and hashes bind declarations but cannot prove intellectual application; record the specialist's actual effect in its contribution and have the independent Reviewer inspect it. New pending records declare the current selection/discovery schemas with an intentionally incomplete receipt. Before execution admission, the gate rebuilds the authoritative packaged catalogue and search index, reruns the recorded initial/refined query, and rejects missing, stale or inconsistent receipts. Discovery is part of the policy/review binding: changing a reconciled query, shortlist or selection after criticism requires current criticism and briefing bindings again. Read-only catalogue inspection may still parse a legacy selection, but --execution cannot admit it until reconciliation. Actual workers and authors Field Meaning --- --- roster.coordinatorId Actual coordinating identity; never also a worker. roster.workers Actual distinct id , role , status: running completed failed , observed spawn/result evidence . roster.assignments Exact {assignmentId, workerId} bindings only after observed dispatch; one binding per assignment. roster.plannedWorkers Queued role / phaseIds ; contributes zero actual/active workers. roster.profiles Complete bundled profile name and actual applying ownerId ; expertise adds zero agents. roster.activeAgentCount Exactly one coordinator plus currently running workers. Completed/failed workers add zero. progress.currentPhase Actual selected current phase. progress.phases One row per phase: id , status , ownerId , authorIds , evidence , workHash ; blocked rows also explain reason . progress.resultRevision Null before stable output; then exact current source/artifact revision or manifest hash, separate from plan/work hash. An unlaunched future assignment stays unbound. Required assignments can run sequentially with one free child slot; a previous worker's real completed result is retained. Do not invent actual IDs or mark completed agents running to satisfy a count. A pending worker can be legitimate at an earlier gate, but every due assigned operation must actually finish before dependent work. Track every substantive author in each phase's authorIds , not just the primary owner. Adopted architecture/UI/plan decisions and source/test/docs/integration changes include secondary authors and coordinator authors. Raw factual evidence, ordinary critical comments or unadopted suggestions do not automatically create downstream authorship. Authoring contributions must match the recorded authors. Profile changes do not change identity or remove independence constraints. Phase kinds remain capture , plan , critique , execute , verify , report , other . Scopes remain read-only , record-only , test-output-only , none , repo-write-scoped , tests-only , docs-only , external-write . The last four require actual mutation authority; a record declaration does not grant external permission. Preparation phases cannot write product. Statuses are pending , in-progress , complete , blocked . A completed phase needs current bound evidence and completed prerequisites. One portable current phase can contain several workers with disjoint assignments. Mark every actual author as that work occurs. Useful contributions and current results workflowContract.contributions contains completed contribution rows: Replace example identities/hashes with actual evidence. Kinds are authoring , investigation , independent-review , verification ; dispositions are incorporated , rejected , unresolved . Required limitations is a unique list of substantive known limits; [] means none are known. Missing/placeholder limits are invalid. Describing an unmet required criterion does not waive it. A rejected suggestion can be useful when the concrete reason/effect is recorded; unresolved in-scope work blocks completion/publication and cannot count as a resolved second contribution. A completed assigned phase needs a current contribution for every assignment. Incorporated authoring workers appear in authorIds ; non-coordinator substantive authors have actual authoring contributions. Coordinator authorship is explicit but adds zero worker contributions. Status-only pings, summaries without inspected evidence, failed workers and repeated identities do not count. Runtime validation rejects structural gaps; substantive usefulness still requires real inspection. Task completion needs at least two distinct useful actual workers and all required assignments resolved. Broad Build uses distinct Architect/Builder/Reviewer; design Build uses distinct UI Director/Builder/Reviewer; shared UI uses four; substantial verification adds a distinct Verifier. Secondary compatible authoring duties may share a worker when these identity and independence requirements still hold. A worker never needs its own recursive team for an already assigned duty. Final acceptance and its required substantial-verification contributions bind resultRevision to progress.resultRevision ; the required Verifier contribution uses kind: verification . Required family coverage comes from a completed, resolved contribution for that family’s actual duty, not an actor’s unrelated earlier contribution or a future assignment. The separate Verifier must complete the selected prerequisite before acceptance; later installation readback may remain pending until installation. Changing the integrated output reopens affected acceptance even with an unchanged plan. A previously returned contribution is reused only when its work and evidence remain current. Keep author checks and independent acceptance distinct. Publication waits for exact prepared-result acceptance and due contributions; future readback assignments run after the external action they inspect. Criticism and bindings A completed review has status: complete , decision: ready revised , actual authorId and reviewerId , truthful mode , exact binding , concrete checks , resolved findings (or grounded noFindingsRationale ) and real report evidence .
